Kindle Direct Publishing: the complete help guide

Every help article Amazon publishes for KDP authors, arranged for reading straight through

2026-08-04

Kindle Direct Publishing: the complete help guide

This guide gathers the help Amazon publishes for people self-publishing through Kindle Direct Publishing: 257 articles across 34 categories, in Amazon’s own words, gathered on 04 August 2026. It covers setting up an account and the tax questionnaire, identity verification and account security, preparing a manuscript and a cover, title setup and pricing, royalties and payments, KDP Select and Kindle Unlimited, paperbacks and hardcovers, distribution and marketing, and the reports.

The reader here is the author. KDP’s user is the self-publisher, so everything written for someone publishing their own book is in scope.

16 documents are not in this guide. Amazon publishes them as PDFs alongside its help pages – the Kindle Publishing Guidelines, the per-language conversion notes, the Goodreads author guides. They are real documentation and they are not pages; they were gathered and set aside rather than quietly dropped.

The KDP Community forum is deliberately absent: it is other authors talking, not Amazon’s own guidance.

Account & Taxes

CreateSpace Account

CreateSpace Account

We’ve moved all CreateSpace books to KDP. To continue working on your books, visit this page and follow the steps to access your books on KDP. - Where are my books? Which email do I use on KDP to access my books? Common KDP Questions How do I access my historical CreateSpace reports on KDP? What if I had a book in process on CreateSpace? Differences between CreateSpace and KDP. Is anything changing about my agreement with CreateSpace?

Where are my books?
  1. Go to CreateSpace.
  2. Enter your CreateSpace email address and click Submit.
  3. This will send an email with a link to your CreateSpace account email address.
  4. Follow the link in the email.
  5. Sign in to KDP to link your KDP account, or create a new account.
  6. Enter the Token you received in the email. Token will be available for 15 mins.
  7. Confirm you’ve selected the correct KDP account and click Take me to my books.
  8. When we are done preparing your account, you’ll be sent to your KDP Bookshelf.
Which email do I use on KDP to access my books?

If you have a KDP account, sign in to that account. If you are new to KDP and don’t have a KDP account, you can create one. You do not need to set up a new KDP account with your CreateSpace login if you already have a KDP account. - How Can I Order Book Copies? Proof Copies Author Copies Manage Orders

How Should I Format My Book? Prepare Your Book

Are Formatting Services Available? Publishing Service Providers & Resources How Can I Update My Published Book? Update Your Book Details Unpublishing and Deleting Books Linking Your eBook and Paperback

How do I access my historical CreateSpace reports on KDP?
  1. Go to your reports
  2. If your sales are within the last 90 days, go to the Sales Dashboard tab. The default is set to 30 days, so adjust it to see the 90-day timeframe
  3. If your sales are older than 90 days, go to the Historical tab
  4. For both reports:

Choose the “All Marketplace” drop-down to filter by marketplace. 5. Choose the “Life to Date” drop-down to see all sales or choose the timeframe

What if I had a book in process on CreateSpace?
  • CreateSpace status: KDP status after moving
  • Incomplete: Draft
  • In Review: Draft
  • Proof Review: Draft
  • Awaiting Proof: Draft
  • Available: Live
  • Retired: Unpublished
Differences between CreateSpace and KDP
  • Payment schedule: CreateSpace paid royalties every month, approximately 30 days after the end of the month in which they were earned. KDP pays royalties every month, approximately 60 days after the end of the month in which they were earned. Example: for royalties earned in November, you’ll be paid in January. This applies as long as the royalties meet the minimum threshold. Expanded Distribution royalties are paid 60 days after the end of the month in which our distributors report their sales.
  • Ordering author copies: When ordering copies of your book on KDP, your order is placed through the Amazon cart and uses Amazon order tracking. Also, copies for the U.K. and the rest of Europe are manufactured and shipped from within Europe. To order copies on KDP, your book must be available on Amazon. Learn more about Author Copies.
  • Unsupported languages: KDP supports books with content and details written in these languages. Published books in unsupported languages from CreateSpace continue to be available for sale on Amazon. It isn’t possible to update or publish new books in unsupported languages. If your unsupported language book moved to KDP in a draft stage, you will need to publish it in a supported language. That said, we continue to evaluate which features and services we offer in the future, including supported languages.
  • Cover Creator: We moved your CreateSpace files and can print your book using your existing Cover Creator cover. If you want to update your cover after the move to KDP, you’re welcome to design a new one using KDP’s Cover Creator. You can also use our templates.
  • Expanded Distribution: On CreateSpace, it wasn’t required to make your book available on Amazon to enable Expanded Distribution. On KDP, it’s required. CreateSpace books that aren’t available for sale on Amazon.com are no longer enrolled in Expanded Distribution.

To re-enroll in Expanded Distribution, make your books available for sale on Amazon.com by publishing and enabling Expanded Distribution through the KDP Bookshelf. It can take six to eight weeks for your book to become available again in Expanded Distribution channels. Learn more about Expanded Distribution. - Author bio: The author bio you entered on CreateSpace continues to display on your book’s detail page. You can manage your bio on Author Central. Don’t have an Author Central account? - Printing costs: On KDP, some low-page count books being printed in Europe (color books less than 30 pages and black-and-white books under 110 pages) will see an increase in printing costs. This affects a small number of titles. Use this calculator to determine printing costs. - Content and quality review: On KDP, if you update your book details (e.g., title, description, categories), manuscript and cover files, or publishing and territory rights, we’ll review the updated version to ensure it meets our guidelines for book details, content, and quality.

Tax Information

Tax Information

Do I have to pay taxes on my KDP sales?
  • An individual who is a U.S. citizen or U.S. resident alien
  • A partnership, corporation, company, or association created or organized in the U.S. or under the laws of the U.S.
  • Any estate (other than a foreign estate)
  • A domestic trust (as defined in Regulations section for Forms W-9 not required to be signed 301.7701-7)

Account security and avoiding scams

Account security and avoiding scams

Keep your account secure
  • Enable two-step verification on your Amazon account.
  • Use a strong, unique password made up of numbers, letters, and symbols. Avoid using publicly available information in your password.
  • Check that the email address and the mobile number that you use to sign in to your account are correct. Learn how to change your email address or account information.
Avoid scams and attempts to steal your information
Key points to remember:
  • KDP does not ask you to reveal your Amazon password or full bank account details. You should only submit this information through your Amazon, KDP, or Author Central account.
  • KDP is a free self-publishing service. We do not offer fee-based services such as editing or book design. Therefore we won’t ask you for payment details such as credit card numbers, PINs, or credit card security codes to bill you for those types of services.
  • For security reasons, KDP customer service does not share account creation dates.
  • Whether by phone, email, or postal mail, larger traditional publishers and movie studios (and directors) rarely approach authors out of the blue with incredible opportunities.
  • Look carefully at the sender’s email address. Some scammers create domain names that resemble those of legitimate publishers. Confirm domain name accuracy by going to the legitimate publisher’s website for comparison.
  • Investigate all supposed “opportunities” that you may be offered. Please feel free to contact KDP with any questions about such opportunities, as well as posting and asking other authors in our KDP online community.

Add my bank account
  1. Go to your KDP account.
  2. Complete two-step verification.
  3. Under Getting Paid, click Add a bank account.
  4. Choose your country or region of residence and click OK.
  5. The next field(s) will vary depending on your bank’s location. Refer to the additional bank information fields table below for guidance.
  6. Enter the account holder Date of Birth. If you signed up as a corporation, enter the Date of Incorporation for the entity listed in the Account holder name field** under Getting Paid**.
  7. In the Account holder name box, enter the name of the person or entity associated with the bank account.
  8. Add the Account holder address. You can choose Select Existing Address or Enter a New Address. This address should match the address your bank has on file.
  9. Click Add.
  10. Scroll down to the bottom and click Save.
  • Field: Definition: Bank Location
  • Account number: Appears on the bottom of your check as a second set of numbers.: US, CA, BR, ZA, IN, JP, AU, NZ
  • Routing number: This nine-digit code appears as the first set of numbers on the bottom of your checks. Your bank can also provide this number to you.: US
  • Bank Code: Numerical code that identifies a bank or branch.: CA, BR, JP
  • Branch Code: Branch codes are codes on checks and bank cards, usually next to the account number.: CA, BR, JP
  • BIC/SWIFT code: This code is available by contacting your bank.: MX, BR, AU, NZ, EU, UK, ID
  • BSB Code: This is Bank/branch number used as the sort/routing code.: ZA, AU
  • IFSC code: An IFSC code, or Indian Financial System Code, is an 11-character alphanumeric code that identifies a bank branch in India.: IN
  • IBAN Number: The International Bank Account Number is an internationally agreed upon system of identifying bank accounts.: EU, UK, OM
  • Account number (CLABE): The CLABE (Clave Bancaria Estandarizada) is an 18-digit number that uniquely identifies account holders and guarantees the correct posting of the payments transfer. The receiver can identify his or her CLABE as it appears on the customer’s bank account statement or it can also be obtained directly from the customer’s bank.: MX
Change my bank account
Delete my bank account
  1. Go to your KDP account.
  2. Choose the option on how you want to receive the one-time password (OTP).
  3. Follow the instructions for two-step verification
  4. After you receive the OTP, enter it and click OK.
  5. Click Getting Paid.
  6. Delete your existing bank account by clicking Delete under the account’s name. Please note this bank account will remain under Deletion pending until you add a new bank account. This to ensure we can always pay for pending royalties.
  7. Under Getting Paid, click Add another bank account, and follow the prompts to add bank information.
  8. Click Add to save information. You will be notified with a green check that you’ve added your bank successfully.
  9. Click Save.
Requirements for adding a bank account

  • When you enter the account holder name, include a space between your first and last name.

  • The account holder name field must contain at least 2 words separated by a space and a minimum of 2 characters per word.

  • The account holder name cannot include initials at the beginning or end. For example, John D or J. Doe are not accepted. Initials in the middle are accepted, for example, John D. Doe.

  • The account holder name cannot be only numbers, special characters, or begin with a special character (symbols that are not letters or numbers).

  • The account holder name cannot be one of the following or similar words: NOT STATED, N/A, N, NULL, VOID, ONE OF OUR CUSTOMERS, NOT PROVIDED, NOT AVAILABLE, NOT APPLICABLE.

  • The account holder name cannot be an email address.

  • Do not include Mr., Ms., Mrs., Dr., etc. as part of the account holder name.

  • When you add or update your address, make sure it is valid. In the pop-up window, you may see an option to select the address you entered or a suggested address.

  • The Address line 1 field must contain at least 2 letters in the Latin alphabet (A-Z).

  • The City and state/province/region field must contain at least two characters. Use the Latin alphabet (A-Z) and numbers (0-9), or a combination of both.

Book Status

Book Status

Book status and definitions
  • Book Status: Definition
  • Draft: You’ve started entering book details, but haven’t submitted your book for publication. While in Draft, you can edit your details at any time.
  • In Review : Once you’ve submitted your book for publication it goes into review. During review, we check your book to make sure it meets our formatting and content guidelines. If your book was In Review and is back in Draft, it means we found some things that need to be updated. Check your email for more details from our team. After you’ve updated your book to meet our guidelines, you can resubmit it for publication and we’ll review it again. While your book is In Review, you won’t be able to make changes. Reviews can’t be expedited or canceled.
  • Publishing: Your book has passed review and is being published. While your book is in Publishing you won’t be able to make changes.
  • Live: Your book is published and available for purchase on Amazon. If needed, you can edit certain book details. For more information on which details can be edited after publishing, visit our Update Your Book Details page.
  • Live - with unpublished changes: You edited the details of your Live book, but haven’t submitted your updates for publication. To submit your updates, follow the steps on our Update Your Book Details page. All updates must pass review before they’re Live on Amazon.
  • Live - Updates in review: Your book is available for purchase (Live), but the recent changes you made are being reviewed and are not yet published. The review process can’t be expedited or canceled. You also won’t be able to make any additional changes at this time. For information on when updates will be published, visit our Timelines page.
  • Live - Updates publishing: Your book is available for purchase (Live), but the recent changes you made are still being published and will be available on Amazon shortly. You won’t be able to make any additional changes until this process is complete.
  • ** Blocked**: Your book doesn’t meet our content guidelines and is blocked from publishing or editing. Blocked titles can’t be deleted from your Bookshelf. If you have concerns about your blocked title, pleasecontact us for more information.
  • Pre-order: Visit our pre-order status page for a complete list of pre-order statuses.
  • Release Date: Visit our release date status page for a complete list of release date statuses.

Create a KDP Account

Create a KDP Account

  1. Go to https://kdp.amazon.com

  2. Under Sign in with your Amazon account, click Sign in.

  3. Enter your email address and password, then click Sign in.

  4. After you’ve successfully logged into your account you’ll be directed to your KDP Bookshelf.

  5. Go to KDP, and click Sign up.

  6. Click Create your KDP account.

  7. Enter your name, email address, and a secure password.

  8. Select a Business type (individual or corporation).

  9. Add your first and last name or the name of your publishing company. Don’t enter your pen name or include special characters (e.g. & ! ? #). If you want to use a pen name, enter it when you’re setting up your book details, see Authors & Contributors for details about how to manage your pen name.

  10. Enter the mailing address you want us to use for tax reporting purposes and royalty payments. Make sure the address provided is valid. In the pop-up window, you may see an option to select the address you provided or our suggested address.

  11. Click Save.

  12. Go to your KDP account.

  13. Complete two-step verification.

  14. Under Getting Paid, click Add a bank account.

  15. Enter your bank account information according to your country/region requirements. Check Add my bank account

  16. Click Add to save information. You will be notified with a green check that you’ve added your bank successfully.

  17. Click Save.

  18. Go to Your Account.

  19. Select Tax Information.

  20. Click Complete Tax Profile.

  21. Respond to the requested information. Save and submit the form.

I set up my bank account, but I haven’t received any payments.

I set up my bank account, but I haven’t received any payments.

When troubleshooting payment issues, it’s important to first troubleshoot the bank details on your KDP account. If you notice payments are not going through, go to Your Account > Getting Paid and review your bank details. If there’s an error, it typically means there’s incorrect information being used, such as a wrong account number or a bank account that doesn’t match your name. To fix common bank issues, you’ll need to first delete and add updated bank details. Before starting this process, make sure you have the correct account and routing numbers. Then double-check that the name you enter matches the name you used with the bank. ##### To update your bank details 1. Go to Your Account > Getting Paid. 2. If needed, follow the instructions for two-step verification. 3. Under the impacted bank account, select Delete account. 4. Complete the steps for removing the bank account. It’ll remain pending until you add another bank account, so payments can process. 5. Click Add another bank account and complete those steps. 6. When done, hit Add. Then click Save at the bottom of the page.

If payments were put on hold, but I updated my bank account, when will I be paid?

Payments that were placed on hold due to an issue with your bank details, will be re-issued once your bank details are verified. It may take a few business days to process, but you can check your Payments report for more details.

Payment Service Provider Program FAQ

Payment Service Provider Program FAQ

Learn about Amazon’s Payment Service Provider Program, including eligibility requirements and trouble-shooting details. ##### What is the Payment Service Provider Program? To continue to provide authors and publishers with a trustworthy publishing experience, we launched the Payment Service Provider Program to limit the types of bank accounts that we accept for the disbursement of KDP royalties. KDP authors who are eligible to use a Payment Service Provider (PSP) may receive their royalties to a bank account issued by a PSP that participates in Amazon’s Payment Service Provider Program (see list of participating PSPs) or to a bank account opened directly with a deposit-taking bank. KDP authors who are not eligible to use a PSP may only receive their royalties to a bank account opened directly with a deposit-taking bank (e.g., HSBC, First National Bank, Bank of America). ##### How do I know if I’m using a Payment Service Provider (PSP)? You are using a PSP if the bank account you entered in your KDP account is managed by a payment company instead of directly issued to you by a deposit-taking bank (i.e., is a traditional bank account). ##### How do I know if I’m eligible to use a PSP? You are eligible to use a PSP if you currently use one or update your bank account to a PSP and do not receive a request to use a deposit-taking bank. You are not eligible to use a PSP if you receive an email notification from KDP informing you that only accounts opened directly with deposit-taking banks are allowed.This notification will also appear in the Getting Paid section of your KDP account, (see Troubleshooting Common Bank Account Errors). If you receive this notification, your royalty payments may be placed on hold and you will be unable to publish on KDP until you update to an eligible bank account. ##### How do I know if I need to provide another bank account or take additional action? If you need to provide an updated bank account or take other actions connected to the Payment Service Provider Program for the disbursement of KDP royalties and to continue to publish on KDP, we’ll notify you. If you need to update your bank account, follow the instructions on this Help article. ##### What if I continue using an ineligible bank account? If we ask you to update your bank account and you do not, you won’t be able to receive royalty payments or publish on KDP. ##### I am currently using a PSP with no issues. Do I have to take any action? If your KDP account does not show a bank account error message in the Getting Paid section, no action is required. If you update your banking information in the future, you’ll need to adhere to all payment requirements, including Amazon’s Payment Service Provider Program requirements. ##### How do I switch to a participating PSP? If you are eligible to use a PSP and need to switch to a participating PSP, follow these steps: 1. Choose one of the currently participating PSPs 2. Visit the participating PSP website of your choice, follow the instructions to apply for a bank account that supports your currencies, and complete the verification process required by the PSP. 3. Once you’ve obtained the new bank account from a participating PSP and provided whatever information or documents your PSP requires in order to complete the required know-your-customer (KYC) verification, go to the Getting Paid section of your KDP account to update your bank account information. 4. Provide any additional documentation that may be required by KDP to complete your bank account update process.

I understand PSPs must perform know-your-customer (KYC) verification and other risk management checks before I can use the bank account. How do I know if my PSP has completed them?

You can find your KYC status in your PSP account or by contacting your PSP directly. Your KDP Getting Paid section will indicate if there is pending verification action. To learn more about pending verification action with your PSP, visit Payment Service Provider Program Risk Management Controls. ##### I’ve provided all the know-your-customer (KYC) information required by my PSP and my PSP has confirmed that no further steps are required. When will this be reflected on KDP? It can take up to 24 hours for your participating PSP’s verification review result to reflect on KDP. If you still see the error message noting that your bank is requesting additional verification in your Getting Paid section after 24 hours, contact your PSP directly to ensure the result has been published to Amazon’s Payment Service Provider Program. If your PSP confirms that they have already published the verification review result to Amazon and it’s been more than 24 hours, you can contact KDP Customer Service. ##### What if my participating PSP never completes the know-your-customer (KYC) verification? If your PSP does not complete the required KYC verification within 45 days after you received the email notification from KDP, you won’t be able to receive royalty payments to that bank account or publish on KDP until the verification review is completed or you switch your payment method to a deposit-taking bank. Note: Your PSP may require additional information or documents from you in order to complete this required step. Please contact your PSP directly for more information. ##### Whom should I contact for support if I have question about my bank account? For issues with your bank account, please contact your bank directly. If you have confirmed your bank account is issued by a participating PSP but you still have issues using it as your KDP bank account, you can contact KDP Customer Support. ##### How does Amazon work with participating PSPs in this program? Participating PSPs must have appropriate risk management controls in place and work with Amazon to reduce the potential for fraud and abuse. For more information, visit Payment Service Provider Program Updates.

Payment Service Provider Program Risk Management Controls

Payment Service Provider Program Risk Management Controls

Amazon requires Payment Service Providers (PSPs) participating in Amazon’s Payment Service Provider Program to implement know-your-customer (KYC), sanctions and denied party screening, anti-money laundering, and other risk management controls. Your disbursements may be delayed as permitted under applicable law until your PSP has completed these required steps. Contact your PSP directly if your disbursements are delayed for this reason or update your bank account to a deposit-taking bank. Visit Payment Service Provider FAQ for additional details on the Payment Service Provider Program and its requirements.

Sign in Issues

Sign in Issues

Sign-in Issues

If you’re experiencing issues logging into your KDP account or forgot your password, you can use the below troubleshooting steps to assist. ##### Contents - Access your account - Forgot your password - Sign-in issues - My Bookshelf is empty - Browser errors - Two-Step Verification Issues

Access your account

To log into your KDP account, follow these instructions: 1. Sign in to KDP. 2. Click Your Account at the top of the page. 3. Follow the instructions for two-step verification. 4. Once you’ve successfully passed two-step verification, your account page will open.

If you log into your KDP and you don’t see your books, make sure you logged in with the correct email address. People often tend to log into their regular Amazon account for shopping instead of their KDP-associated account. To fix this, use the email address for the KDP account you published books under. Moved from CreateSpace? Learn which email to use on KDP to access your books. ##### Forgot your password If you’ve forgotten your password, you can reset it by going through our password assistance process. Follow these steps: 1. Go to https://kdp.amazon.com/ and click Sign in. 2. Click Need help? and then Forgot your password?. This will open the password assistance window. 3. Enter the email address or phone number associated with the KDP account you published books with. 4. Enter the one-time password (OTP) verification number. 5. You may be asked to verify account information, such as your zip code or credit card expiration date. 6. Create a new password.

If you have trouble receiving the one-time password (OTP), please read our Two-Step Verification article. As soon as you’ve created a new password, it’s active. ##### Sign-in issues - Email Address: Your email address must be in the format username@domain.com (or .net, .org, etc.). If you have more than one email address, make sure you’re using the correct email address and password combination. - Mobile Phone Number: If you created your account with a mobile phone number, you’ll need to use your mobile phone number to log into your account. Make sure that you’re including your country code in your mobile phone number. - Password: Check CAPS Lock and NUM Lock on your keyboard. Passwords are case sensitive, so “PASSWORD” and “Password” are recognized as two different passwords. If you’re sure you’re using the correct email address or mobile phone number, try our Password Reset page. If you don’t receive an email from Amazon, check your Junk or Spam folder. - Multiple Accounts: Sometimes multiple accounts are created if you visit Amazon and accidentally indicate that you’re a new customer when you sign in. This creates another account with the same email address and a different password. To fix this, sign out of the current account and then sign back in again with the email and password associated with your KDP account. - Locked Amazon Account: If you have tried to sign in to your Amazon account on the Store too many times using an incorrect password, tried to access the account using a new device, or answered the security questions incorrectly, you can get locked out of your Amazon account. To fix this, contact Amazon Customer Service to unlock your account. After your Amazon account is unlocked, you should be able to sign in to KDP.

Taking photos of your ID

Taking photos of your ID

Tips
  1. Choose a room with plenty of natural lighting instead of using a camera flash. It’s best to take the photo during the daytime.
  2. Position the camera directly above the ID. Make sure all four corners of the ID are visible and your shadow doesn’t cover any details.
  3. Hold the camera at an adequate distance to see details on the ID (i.e. full name, barcodes, ID numbers). Don’t hold it too far away, where information is illegible, and not too close where the ID gets cropped.
  4. Take separate photos of the front and back of the ID following the guidelines above.
Granting browser permission to take a photo
Checklist for avoiding errors
  • Mistake: Incorrect: Correct
  • Blurry photo If your ID looks blurry, move the ID towards your camera until the image is in focus.: (image: blurry photo): (image: info cut off)
  • Information is cut off Make sure the entire ID is visible, including barcodes. All four corners of the ID should be clearly seen.: (image: info cut off)
  • Glare or shade on the photo If areas are too shiny or dark and make the photo hard to read, try adjusting the lighting or moving to another spot. Make sure to position the camera directly above the ID.: (image: photo glare)
  • Camera is too far away from ID Only the ID should be present in the photo, no other objects. Make sure the focus is close enough to read text.: (image: image too far away)

Troubleshooting common bank account errors

Troubleshooting common bank account errors

Bank account validation can fail for multiple reasons. Below are common bank account error messages and how to fix them. If you need to update your bank account, follow the instructions on this Help article. For security purposes, you will need to delete the existing bank account and then add the corrected banking details. Once you’ve updated your bank account details, we’ll check the information provided (name, account number, routing number, and/or IBAN number) within five business days to confirm we can make payments to your account. If we can’t validate your bank details, we’ll send you an email with additional information. ##### Common error messages - We currently don’t support this Payment Service Provider (PSP). Please remove and add an eligible bank account to receive payments and continue publishing on KDP. - Your bank is requesting additional verification before we can issue payments. Sign into your payment provider account and review their request to receive payments and continue publishing on KDP. - Invalid bank details were added. Please remove this bank account and add a corrected version. - A new routing number or bank details may be required. To update, remove this bank account and add a corrected version. - Only accounts from deposit-taking banks are allowed. Please remove and add an eligible bank account.

We currently don’t support this Payment Service Provider (PSP). Please remove and add an eligible bank account to receive payments and continue publishing on KDP.

The Payment Service Provider (PSP) in your KDP account does not participate in Amazon’s Payment Service Provider Program. You need to update your bank account to an eligible PSP or to an account issued directly to you from a deposit-taking bank (i.e., is a traditional bank account) to publish on KDP and receive royalties. ##### Your bank is requesting additional verification before we can issue payments. Sign into your payment provider account and review their request to receive payments and continue publishing on KDP. This error message shows when you need to complete the required know-your-customer (KYC) verification with your Payment Service Provider (PSP). You can find your KYC status in your PSP account or by contacting your PSP directly. For more information, visit Payment Service Provider Program Risk Management Controls. ##### Invalid bank details were added. Please remove this bank account and add a corrected version. This error message appears when invalid bank information is added to your KDP account that cannot be verified. Examples of invalid bank information could be an incorrect account/routing number or BIC/SWIFT code. To address this error, add the corrected bank information to your account in the impacted marketplaces. If you need to verify your bank information, please contact your bank directly. Once you’ve updated your bank information, we’ll deposit any past due payments on the next scheduled payment date. ##### A new routing number or bank details may be required. To update, remove this bank account and add a corrected version. Sometimes an internal change in your bank means it won’t accept future payments from KDP using your existing bank information. Your account might require a new routing number or other banking details. If you receive this error, verify your bank information directly with your bank and add the corrected information to your account for the impacted marketplaces. Once you’ve updated your bank account information, we’ll attempt to process any payments in the next payment cycle. ##### Only accounts from deposit-taking banks are allowed. Please remove and add an eligible bank account. KDP may ask you to update your bank details to a deposit-taking bank in order to publish on KDP. If you receive this error message, Payment Service Providers (PSPs) are not supported for your account and you will need to add a bank account that you opened directly with a bank, e.g., a checking or savings account from HSBC, First National Bank, Bank of America, or your local bank. To verify if your bank account qualifies, ask yourself whether you can directly deposit cash into your account at a physical location or using an automated teller machine (ATM). Both personal and business bank accounts from deposit-taking banks are eligible. If you are prompted to update your banking information to a deposit-taking bank and you have different bank accounts saved for different marketplaces, you must ensure all bank accounts meet the eligibility requirements.

Enable two-step verification
  1. Go to the Login & security page of your Amazon customer account.
  2. Select Edit beside Two-Step Verification (2SV) Settings.
  3. Click Get Started.
  4. Follow the on-screen instructions.
  • This means the next time you sign in to Amazon (to shop, manage orders, etc.), you will also be asked for a security code (OTP).
  • You don’t need to set it up twice, one setup works for both accounts.
How to sign in with two-step verification
  1. Sign in to your KDP account using your email address and password.
  2. Choose how you like to receive the one-time password (OTP). Note: If the last three digits of the number listed aren’t correct, select Two-step Verification Account Recovery.
  3. Based on the choice of delivery, you will receive a phone call or text message with a six digit unique code.
  4. Enter your unique code in and click Sign in.
  5. Once you’ve completed two-step verification, your account page will open.
Add or edit your phone number for two-step verification
  1. Go to the Login & security page of your Amazon customer account.
  2. Select Manage beside Two-Step Verification (2SV) Settings.
  3. In the Enrolled 2SV Authenticators section, you can:
  4. Check which phone number or numbers are used for two-step verification
  5. Update a phone number by clicking Change
  6. Remove a phone number by clicking Remove
  7. Add a phone number by clicking Add new phone or Authenticator App. You can add up to 2 phone numbers. Learn how to add an authenticator app.
I want to disable two-step verification from my KDP account
I can’t access the phone number?
I don’t have a cell signal or can’t get calls or texts?
Authenticator App
How do I download an authenticator app or extension?
  • Smartphones or mobile devices. Go to the app store and search for “authenticator app”. Search results will show third-party apps such as Google Authenticator and Microsoft Authenticator. You can use any app you want.
  • Desktop computers. Use a search engine to find an authenticator extension (add-on) that works with your browser. For example, if you use Firefox, go to Firefox ADD-ONS, or if you use Chrome, go the Chrome Webstore, and search for “authenticator” in the search box. Choose an add-on from the available options and click “Add to Firefox” or “Add to Chrome” depending on your browser.
How do I add an authenticator app or extension to my Amazon account?
  1. Go to the Login & security page of your Amazon customer account.
  2. Select Edit beside Two-Step Verification (2SV) Settings.
  3. If this is your first time adding an authentication preference, click Get Started. If you’ve previously added an authentication method, in the Enrolled 2SV Authenticators section, click Add new phone or Authenticator App.
  4. Choose Authenticator App and follow the instructions that appear.
Troubleshoot OTP Issues
What if I don’t receive an OTP?
  • Make sure you have a good cell or WiFi signal.
  • Check that you’ve provided us with the correct phone number.
  • Click Didn’t receive the OTP? and get a new OTP via a different phone number or method.
  • Ask your mobile service provider if there are restrictions that prevent you from receiving codes.
  • Try an authenticator app like Google Authenticator and Microsoft Authenticator.
What if I get an error that says the OTP isn’t valid?
  • Check that the OTP you entered matches the OTP we sent you.
  • Try to enter the OTP again. If you’re using an authenticator app, wait for the OTP to expire. When a new OTP generates, enter the new OTP.
  • Click Didn’t receive the OTP? and get a new OTP via a different phone number or method.
  • After you receive the OTP, make sure to enter it within 10 minutes.
  • If you receive multiple OTPs, make sure to enter the newest one.
What if I get an error that says you can’t call me?
How do I change from calls to texts?
  1. Go to the Login & security page of your Amazon customer account.
  2. Select Edit beside Two-Step Verification (2SV) Settings.
  3. In the Enrolled 2SV Authenticators section, click Add new phone or Authenticator App
  4. Complete two-step verification by receiving an OTP via voice call
  5. Enter the OTP you received and the Add backup method page will open
  6. Choose Text message and enter your phone number. This can be the same number you used for voice calls, or a different number.
  7. Click Send OTP to get a code via text message
  8. Enter the OTP you received and click Verify OTP and continue
Reporting suspicious activity
  • Unexpected 2SV requests
  • Changes to your account you didn’t make
  • Any other signs of unauthorized access
  1. Change your password
  2. Contact KDP support at https://kdp.amazon.com/contact-us
  3. Review your account activity and report any unauthorized changes

How do I know if I need to verify my identity?
Why do I need to verify my identity again?
How do I verify my identity
  1. Log into KDP. Under Your Account, go to Your Identity.
  2. Enter or review your information (e.g. full name, address, date of birth). The name and country in the Your identity section on your account must match the name and country of your government-issued ID. If it does not, update this information in the Your Identity section of your account before verifying your identity. For corporations and non-individual entities (e.g., LLC or agency), enter the details of an authorized representative for your business.
  3. Save your information if you made changes.
  4. Click Verify identity.
  5. Choose an ID type.
  6. Take the required photos of your physical ID. Photos of digital IDs or paper IDs (e.g., an identification document that is printed on paper) of any kind cannot be processed. If you’re using your computer, you can click Continue on another device to switch to your mobile device. You can scan a QR code with your phone’s camera, or receive a secure link to switch devices.
  7. Take a selfie when prompted. Position your face in the camera frame and follow the on-screen prompts.
  8. Click Submit.

What happens when I close my KDP account?

What happens when I close my KDP account?

What happens when I close my KDP account?

Once your KDP account is closed, it is no longer accessible to you, it cannot be restored, we will process your data deletion request, and your agreement to the KDP Terms and Conditions will be terminated. Before closing your account, we recommend you review your account to confirm your name, mailing address, bank account number, and bank routing number are accurate. This ensures that you receive any outstanding royalties, if eligible. Please note that following account closure, we cannot update your banking details or mailing address. You may also wish to download your KDP reports and tax forms, as you will permanently lose access to this information if you close your KDP account. If you close your KDP account, you will not be able to access your KDP account, including: - Account details - Reports - Tax forms - Bookshelf

What happens to my personal information when I close my KDP account?

When you close your KDP account, we will process your data deletion request. However, please be advised that Amazon is legally required or entitled to retain some types of data. We do this in line with applicable laws including for tax, accounting, and fraud prevention purposes. ##### What happens to my live books when I close my KDP account? Once your KDP account is closed, we will unpublish your books. Please note, per our KDP Terms and Conditions, we may continue to sell any inventory we have of your print books, and we may fulfill any customer orders for your print books pending as of the date we confirm your account closure and data deletion request. We may continue to maintain digital copies of your digital books in order to provide continuing access to or re-downloads of your digital books, as well as digital copies of your books to support customers who have purchased your book prior to your account closure and data deletion request. ##### I made a mistake on the request to close my account and need to reverse my decision. This is a permanent action and cannot be reversed. ##### I want to start publishing through KDP again. If you want to publish with us again, you won’t be able to create a KDP account under the same email address. This restriction is due to technical limitations that allow only one account per email address. ##### How do I close my account and request data deletion? For instructions, visit our how to close your KDP account help page. ##### I have an issue with my latest payment. How do I contact KDP since my account is closed? If you attempt to log into your closed KDP account, you will be given the option to contact us. ##### If I want to delete my Amazon account (not KDP account), how do I do that? To close your Amazon account, you can follow the instructions on this Help article and request it through Amazon’s customer service team.

What if my account name or country changes or is different from my ID?

What if my account name or country changes or is different from my ID?

For individuals
  1. Continue to use (or enter) your personal details that match your ID in your KDP account.
  2. Complete the identity verification process.
  3. Once your ID is updated to reflect your new name or address, log into your KDP account. Click Your account > Your identity.
  4. Update your identity details and then re-verify, using your new ID.
For individuals using pen names
For businesses
  1. Log into KDP.
  2. Go to Your account > Your identity.
  3. Update the identity using the details of the current authorized representative.
  4. Verify the identity of that representative using an ID that exactly matches the name and address of the authorized representative in your KDP account (name and written language).
My current address is different than my ID address

Applying for a U.S. EIN for Corporations and Non-Individual Entities

Applying for a U.S. EIN for Corporations and Non-Individual Entities

Instructions for Completing and Submitting Tax Forms - Example Form SS-4, only meant to show a sample of a completed form - How to Apply for an EIN (Official IRS Instructions in English) - Instructions for form SS-4(Official IRS Instructions in English)

The following guidelines do not replace the form instructions, and you should only use them as a supplement to the IRS instructions. Please consult your tax advisor if you require further guidance. Box 1 - 6: Enter the name and address of the company. - Box 1. Enter the legal name of the entity applying for the EIN, in English (required). - Box 2. Enter the trade name of the business if different from the legal name (if applicable). - Box 3. If the entity applying is a trust, estate or has designated a person to receive tax information, enter the name of the trustee, executor/administrator or the “care of” person. Enter the individual’s first name, middle initial, and last name. - Box 4a. Enter your address in the following order, in English:  Room number Building name Street number Street name - Box 4b. Enter your address in the following order, in English:   City Prefecture Postal code Country (do not abbreviate the country name). Please reference the IRS instructions for additional information. - Box 5. Enter the entity’s physical address only if different from its mailing address shown in lines 4a-b. - Box 6. Enter the entity’s primary physical location. For example, if your business is located in Nippon, you may enter “Japan”.

Box 7a – 7b: - Enter the full name of the entity’s responsible party, as defined in the IRS instructions. For example, the responsible party for a business that is a corporation would be the principal officer of the corporation. - Enter the responsible party’s U.S. Social Security Number (SSN), Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN), or Employer Identification Number (EIN), if applicable.

Box 8a. An LLC is an entity organized under the laws of a state or foreign country as a limited liability company and may be treated as a partnership, corporation or be disregarded as an entity separate from its owner. If this application is for an LLC, select “Yes”. - If you select “Yes” to Box 8a, you must complete Box 8b and 8c.

Box 9a: Check the box that best describes the type of entity applying for an EIN. Please reference the IRS instructions for additional information. Box 9b: If a corporation, enter the state or foreign country where the company is incorporated. Box 10: Check the reason for applying. A selection is required and you cannot enter “N/A”. Only check one box. For example, if you are completing the form solely to obtain an EIN to claim a reduced rate of withholding under an income tax treaty, the appropriate box would be “Compliance with IRS withholding requirements.” Box 11: If you are starting a new business, enter the starting date of the business. You may reference the IRS instructions for additional guidance. Box 12: Enter the last month of your accounting year or tax year. You may reference the IRS instructions for additional guidance. For example, a calendar year would have December as the last month. Box 13 - 15: If applicable, please complete any required information. You may reference the IRS instructions for additional guidance. Box 16: Check the one box that best describes the principal activity of the applicant’s business. You must check a box. Please reference the IRS instructions for additional guidance. Box 17: Use Box 17 to describe the applicant’s principal line of business in more detail. An entry is required. You may reference the IRS instructions for additional guidance. Box 18: Check the applicable box which indicates whether or not the applicant entity applying for an EIN was issued an EIN previously. Sign and Date the form - Name and title (type or print clearly): Enter the same name entered in Box 1. - Signature: Print out the application first and sign it in writing (Not electrically). Signature in your local language and script, e.g. Japanese, is acceptable. - Applicants Telephone Number Write your telephone number in this space, with the country code included. If your number is too long to fit in the space electronically, print out the application form and enter the telephone number in writing. - Applicant’s FAX number: Enter your FAX number in the same way you enter the telephone number above, if you decide to fax. If you enter your FAX number, your EIN will be sent to your FAX. If you do not enter your FAX number, your EIN will be sent to your address by mail. It will take a few weeks for it to be delivered to your address.**** - Date: Enter the date of signature in writing in the following order, month, date and year.

International applicants located outside of the United States can apply for an EIN by telephone, fax, or mail. - Telephone. Call the IRS Monday through Friday at +1 (267) 941-1099 (not a toll free number). This is the fastest method and will allow you to receive the EIN immediately. - Fax. If you have no principal business or office in the United States, send the completed Form SS-4 to the IRS at +1 (304) 707-9471 and include your fax number on the application. You should receive a fax within four days listing your EIN. - Mail. Applications processed by mail may take 4 weeks. If this is the best method for you, mail Form SS-4 to this address:  Internal Revenue Service Attn: EIN International Operation Philadelphia, PA 19255

These guidelines do not replace the form instructions, and you should only use them as a supplement to the IRS instructions. Please consult your tax adviser if you require further guidance.

Complete Tax Profile

Complete Tax Profile

Table of Contents - How to complete your tax profile - How to check your tax information status - Tips for non-U.S. publishers

How to complete your tax profile
  1. Sign in to your KDP account at https://kdp.amazon.com
  2. Complete the two-step verification using preferred method
  3. Go to Your Account
  4. Go to Tax Information
  5. Select Complete Tax Profile and enter required details

After submitting your responses, you can check the tax information status by going back to Tax Information in your account page. Validated tax information will show a status of “Complete”. If you previously responded to and completed your tax profile, you can confirm or update details by going to Update/Review Tax Profile. ##### How to check your tax information status 1. Sign in to your KDP account at https://kdp.amazon.com 2. Complete the two-step verification using preferred method 3. Go to Your Account 4. Select Tax Information

Validated tax information will show a status of “Complete.” For more information on your tax account status, refer to What is my tax account status? ##### Tips for non-U.S. publishers ###### Completing tax profile Unless you change the default marketplaces during your title setup, you’ll sell on the U.S. Amazon Marketplace. From those sales, you are paid royalties. Royalties are considered taxable income in the U.S. U.S. tax regulations require Amazon to collect information about the tax identity of content providers under U.S. law. The tax profile page guides you through a step-by-step process to gather all necessary information required to establish your tax identity and generate a Form W-8. The default withholding rate is 30%, but you may be eligible for a reduced rate if your country of tax residence has a tax treaty with the U.S. Check to see if your country has a treaty with the U.S.: United States Income Tax Treaties - A to Z. Please contact the IRS if you have additional tax-related questions. Note: Your W-8 will expire on the last day of the third succeeding calendar year from the date signed. When the form is expired, you will need to update your Tax Profile to generate a new W8-form. If you are currently using a reduced country withholding rate, it will default back to 30% if you allow the W-8 to expire. ###### Tax Identification Number (TIN) A Tax Identification Number or TIN is the number you use to identify yourself with taxing authorities. This could be: - Your country’s Tax Identification Number - An Individual Tax Identification Number (ITIN) - Employer Identification numbers (EIN) for businesses.

Most countries have a tax identification number. If you are unsure if your country has one, contact your local tax authority. If your country doesn’t have any of the three types of TINs mentioned above, you can apply for a U.S. TIN on the IRS website. It can take up to seven weeks to complete this process once your application has been submitted. For more information about U.S. TIN, visit: - Applying for a U.S. TIN (Taxpayer ID Number) - Individual Taxpayer Identification Number - Employer ID Numbers

EU VAT Invoices

EU VAT Invoices

If you reside in an EU Member State and have a registered EU VAT number, you’ll need to provide your EU VAT number when completing your KDP tax profile. After entering your EU VAT number, you must also accept the Amazon Self-Billing agreement to allow Amazon to generate VAT invoices on your behalf and maintain timely payment processing. Note: Providing your VAT number is separate from any tax forms you may have submitted (such as a W-8BEN or W-9 form). - Amazon self-billing agreement - Value Added Tax (VAT) invoices - Download tax invoices - Frequently asked questions

Amazon Self-Billing Agreement

The Amazon Self-Billing Agreement is a formal agreement that establishes the terms between you and Amazon to set out the process for Amazon to generate VAT invoices on your behalf. We’ll ask you to renew the agreement every 10 years, or earlier, if your tax details change. ###### How to view and access the self-billing agreement 1. Sign in to your KDP account: https://kdp.amazon.com 2. Complete two-step verification using preferred method 3. Go to Your Account 4. Go to Tax Information 5. Under the Automated Payments column, click on Self-billing Agreement

A pop-up window will display the agreement’s terms and conditions You must accept the agreement to ensure that VAT invoices are generated on your behalf. Payments issued to you by Amazon Media EU S.à r.l. may be delayed if you do not accept the agreement. You can access and view the Amazon Self-Billing agreement at any time by following the above steps. ##### Value Added Tax (VAT) invoices We’ll process tax invoices after each payment period. These invoices are generated on your behalf and will reflect payments issued by Amazon Media EU S.à r.l. for royalties earned on EU marketplaces. Important: Tax invoices will only be generated for EU-based authors who provide a registered EU VAT number and accept the Amazon Self-Billing Agreement when completing their tax profile. If you don’t provide a registered EU VAT number and accept the Amazon Self-Billing Agreement, tax invoices won’t be generated, even if your payments are issued from Amazon Media EU S.à r.l. ###### How to view your tax invoices 1. Sign in to your KDP account: https://kdp.amazon.com 2. Complete two-step verification using preferred method 3. Go to Your Account, select Tax Invoices 4. You will be redirected to the Tax Invoice dashboard. Within this dashboard, you will see the processed VAT invoices. You can also specify the date range to view your tax invoices.

Note: Tax invoices are securely stored and available to access for 10 years. For example, if the invoice is issued on March 31, 2026, the availability period of that invoice is March 31, 2026 – March 31, 2036. After the 10-year period, you will not be able to access the invoice. ##### Download tax invoices You can securely download individual tax invoices as a PDF file, or bulk download as a spreadsheet. ###### How to download a specific tax invoice 1. Sign in to your KDP account: https://kdp.amazon.com 2. Complete two-step verification using preferred method 3. Go to Your Account, select Tax Invoices 4. Find the specific tax invoice you want to download 5. Select Download. A PDF file will be downloaded

How to bulk download tax invoices
  1. Sign in to your KDP account: https://kdp.amazon.com
  2. Complete two-step verification using preferred method
  3. Go to Your Account, select Tax Invoices
  4. Select Download in the top right corner
  5. Choose the spreadsheet option as a CSV or Excel file for download to view invoice details
Frequently asked questions

Why do I need to provide my EU VAT number?

If you’re VAT registered in an EU Member State and have a VAT registration number issued by an EU tax authority, providing your registered EU VAT number during tax profile submission will allow Amazon to generate VAT invoices on your behalf and maintain timely payments. I’m an individual author without a registered business. Do I need a VAT number?

No. If you are an individual author and do not operate as a registered business, you are not required to have an EU VAT number. VAT registration is a requirement for businesses carrying out taxable activities, not for individual, non-business authors. How can I get an EU VAT number?

The EU VAT number is a unique identification number assigned to businesses by EU tax authorities for VAT purposes. For more information about getting an EU VAT number, please refer to the official European Commission website on VAT identification numbers. If you require additional tax support, please consult your tax advisor. Each EU Member State may have different VAT number requirements. Amazon does not provide tax advisory or compliance services. I don’t live in Luxemburg, am I still required to provide my EU VAT number?

Yes, KDP operates under a multi-party agreement structure in which the ‘Amazon parties’ include Amazon Media EU S.à.r.l., a société à responsabilité limitée organized under the laws of Luxembourg. As such, KDP’s operations within the European Union fall under the jurisdiction of Luxembourg law, and publishers, authors, and associated teams must ensure compliance with applicable Luxembourg and EU regulations. Learn more about Kindle Direct Publishing Terms and Conditions I have previously completed my tax profile. Why do I need to complete my tax profile again?

If you receive payments from Amazon Media EU S.à r.l., you will need to complete your tax profile and provide your EU VAT number (if you have one) for Amazon to be able to generate VAT invoices on your behalf. Learn more about Complete Tax Profile. What is the Amazon Self-Billing Agreement?

The Amazon Self-Billing Agreement is a formal agreement that establishes the terms between you and Amazon to set out the process for Amazon to generate VAT invoices on your behalf, and your obligation to notify us if your tax details change. Do I need to accept the agreement?

Yes, you must accept the Amazon Self-Billing Agreement. If you reside in an EU Member State and provide a registered EU VAT number when completing your tax profile, accepting the agreement is required. Will historical tax invoices also be available to me?

No, historical invoices will not be available. Invoices will be generated on your behalf for future payments made after you accept the Amazon Self-Billing agreement. I accepted the Amazon Self-Billing Agreement, when will I see my invoices?

Tax invoices will be available to view and download every month after your royalties are paid. Learn more about KDP Payments. I’m currently submitting my invoices manually. Do I need to continue doing that after this change?

No. If you provide us with your registered EU VAT number and accept the Amazon Self-Billing Agreement, we’ll issue tax invoices on your behalf automatically. You can access these invoices from your Tax Invoice dashboard. Why does my payment report differ from my tax invoice statements?

Your tax invoice statement may not match your payment report because invoices only reflect payments issued by Amazon Media EU S.à r.l. for royalties earned on EU marketplaces. Will the tax invoices replace my U.S. year-end tax forms?

No. Tax invoices generated won’t replace the U.S. year-end tax forms you receive annually. Learn more about Year End Tax Forms.

Tax Withholding

Tax Withholding

  • If you have a US tax identification number (TIN), you must provide this number when completing your tax profile.

  • If you do not have a US TIN, you may enter the income tax identification number issued to you by the tax authority in your country of residence.

  • Singapore publishers. Royalty payments for sales on Amazon.in are not subject to Singaporean tax withholding once you have provided Amazon with your Singapore taxpayer identification number. Download the Singapore Tax Questionnaire  and complete it, including your Singapore taxpayer identification number, and mail it to the address in the questionnaire.

  • Non-Singapore publishers. Royalty payments for sales on Amazon.in are subject to 10% Singaporean tax withholding. You may qualify for a reduced rate of Singapore tax withholding under the income tax treaty between your country and Singapore. Authors located in the US and India likely do not qualify for a reduced rate. Expected reduced withholding rates can be found in this table.

What is my tax information status?

What is my tax information status?

You may see one of these tax statuses under Tax Information in your KDP Account:

Incomplete

Country-specific tax regulations require Amazon to request information about your tax identity under country-specific law. Your tax status shows “Incomplete” if the required tax profile is not submitted, information provided is out of date, or an issue was detected. Please complete your tax profile as soon as possible. You cannot begin publishing or selling books in the Kindle store or update existing books without a complete tax profile.

Under Review

Your tax profile is submitted and under review. We will let you know if more information is necessary.

Complete

Your KDP account is in good standing. You may publish new books and edit existing ones. In a complete status, you will see the date you submitted your tax profile and the applicable withholding rate.

Processing Paper Forms

You’ve mailed us your paper tax forms, which can take 5-6 weeks to receive and process. If your information changes while your forms are processing, you can submit your tax form electronically by providing your consent to electronic submission when completing your tax profile, which will expedite processing.

Reasons for an Incomplete Status

Amazon does not have insight into the details of why tax information is incomplete, but here are some common issues to watch out for: - If you are submitting a Social Security Number (SSN), use the same name format that appears on your Social Security card. - If you are submitting an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN), use the number issued by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). - If you are submitting an Employer Identification Number (EIN), use the exact same name that appears on the first line of the address header on your Notice CP575A from the IRS. - Misspelling your name, not including your middle initial or middle name, or entering an incorrect Taxpayer Identification Number may cause a mismatch between your tax identity information and IRS Records.

When will I get my tax forms?
  • U.S. publishers. We issue Form 1099-MISC on or before January 31 each year (or the following business day if January 31 falls on a weekend or legal holiday).
  • Non-U.S. publishers. We issue Form 1042-S on or before March 15 each year (or the following business day if March 15 falls on a weekend or legal holiday).
How do I get my forms?

  1. Sign in to KDP and click Your Account at the top of the page.

  2. Follow the instructions for two-step verification.

  3. Select Update/Review Tax Profile.

  4. Find your available tax forms in the Tax statements section.

  5. Under Tax form, click Download for the form you need.

  6. Go to taxcentral.amazon.com.

  7. Use your KDP account sign-in and password.

  8. Find your available tax forms in the Tax statements section.

  9. Under Tax form, click Download for the form you need.

Note: From the tax dashboard, under Your to-do list and alerts, you may also find a download link for your most recent tax form. ##### I’m having issues accessing the forms. ##### Why didn’t I get a tax form? - The forms haven’t been made available or delivered yet. - U.S. publishers. We issue IRS Form 1099-MISC on or before January 31 each year (or the following business day if January 31 falls on a weekend or legal holiday). - Non-U.S. publishers. We issue IRS Form 1042-S on or before March 15 each year (or the following business day if March 15 falls on a weekend or legal holiday). - If you choose paper delivery, forms will be mailed to the address which you provided when you submitted your tax profile. Depending on where you live, forms can take up to two weeks to arrive.

  • U.S. publishers. If you exceeded the $10 global royalty payment threshold across all Amazon businesses, your IRS Form 1099-MISC will be issued on or before January 31 (or the following business day if January 31 falls on a weekend or legal holiday).
  • Non-U.S. publishers. If you exceeded the $0.49 global royalty payment threshold across all Amazon businesses, your IRS Form 1042-S will be issued on or before March 15 (or the following business day if March 15 falls on a weekend or legal holiday).

Do I have to pay taxes on what I earned from selling my KDP books?
  • U.S. publishers. If you exceeded the $10 global royalty payment threshold across all Amazon businesses, you will be subject to IRS Form 1099-MISC reporting. Payments to corporations, including limited liability companies (LLCs) that are treated as C- or S- Corporations, and certain tax-exempt organizations are not reportable on Form 1099-MISC.
  • Non-U.S. publishers. If you exceeded the $0.49 global royalty payment threshold across all Amazon businesses, your IRS Form 1042-S will be issued on or before March 15 (or the following business day if March 15 falls on a weekend or legal holiday). This form is an informational statement that the U.S. taxing authority (called the “Internal Revenue Service” or “IRS”) requires Amazon to provide. The form is sent to non-U.S. publishers who received U.S.-sourced income during the previous calendar year. The amount in Box 2 shows payments received from sales (in USD) from the United States. Box 7 represents any associated U.S. tax withheld from these payments, also in USD. If you have questions, please consult a tax advisor or www.irs.gov.
How do I update my delivery preference?
  1. Sign in to KDP and click Your Account at the top of the page.
  2. Follow the instructions for two-step verification.
  3. Go to Tax Information
  4. Select Update/Review Tax Profile.
  5. Navigate through the questions.
  6. After you click Submit Form, select Change Delivery Preference.
  7. Choose your delivery preference.

Amazon Store & Detail Page

Book Trends Data

Book Trends Data

Book trends data is displayed in search and on detail pages and represents an aggregate number of customers who engage with a title in any format. The data is updated daily and reflects customers that have engaged with your book in the most recent 30 days. Customers qualify through engaging with a title in any of the following ways: - Purchases across all book formats - Kindle eBook reading (including Kindle Unlimited) - Audible listening

Book trends data is not a sales report - it is meant to give an indication of customer engagement - and the numbers you see in your sales report will not be comparable. There is a minimum level of customer activity required for book trends data to appear for your book. So the number you see may increase, change, or no longer display depending on your book’s most recent customer engagement. The criteria for book trends data are the same across all titles. Amazon is continually testing new features for customers and while all books are eligible for this feature, not all customers will see book trends data during the testing period.

Customer Reviews

Customer Reviews

Customer Reviews

Customer reviews help readers discover what others think about your book to inform their purchase decision. The Amazon Community team manages customer reviews, including requests to remove reviews that violate the Community Guidelines. 1. Visit Customer Service. 2. Select Something else. 3. Click Amazon Community. 4. Choose the most appropriate option from the list of Amazon Community features.

Table of Contents
