KDP Publishing: Beta: Audiobooks with virtual voice

Audiobooks with virtual voice eligibility and troubleshooting

Audiobooks with virtual voice eligibility and troubleshooting

Audiobooks with virtual voice eligibility and troubleshooting

To be eligible for an audiobook with virtual voice, your eBook must meet the required criteria. ##### Contents - Checking eligibility - Eligibility criteria and troubleshooting - Format and quality troubleshooting

Checking eligibility

After your eBook is Live, we will complete an eligibility check against the criteria below. If Checking eligibility shows in your KDP Bookshelf, please allow an additional 5 hours after your eBook is Live to view your book’s eligibility status. If Checking eligibility shows more than 5 hours after your eBook moved to Live status, please contact us for further assistance. If your eBook is eligible, the option Add Audible audiobook with virtual voice will appear on your KDP Bookshelf. If you update an ineligible eBook so that it meets the eligibility criteria, the link to create an audiobook should appear on your Bookshelf after the updated eBook is Live and passes the eligibility check. Note: We reserve the right to determine the types of eBooks that we accept in the beta program. We may choose not to accept your eBook for creation of an audiobook or to remove your audiobook from sale at any time. ##### Eligibility criteria and troubleshooting Review requirements for your eBook to be eligible for an audiobook with virtual voice and potential troubleshooting steps below. If your eBook is ineligible, check the reason(s) listed by selecting Why isn’t my eBook eligible? on your KDP Bookshelf. - Your eBook must: How to correct - have a Live status: Your eBook must be Live before you will have the option to create an audiobook with virtual voice. Your eBook’s status cannot be Publishing. Note that eBooks available for pre-order are not eligible.

For more information on publishing timelines, visit Book Status. - hold worldwide or U.S. distribution rights: To be eligible, your eBook must be enabled for either All territories (worldwide rights), or United States must be enabled for individual territories.

For more information, visit eBook Distribution Rights. - be suitable for an audiobook: Consider the types of books that are best suited for audio. Your eBook must not be empty or have empty chapters. Books with a lot of picture content that contain images, tables, graphs, or code excerpts may not provide a great listener experience. For example, cookbooks or comic books would generally not provide the best listener experience. - be reflowable (not a fixed format): To be eligible, your eBook must be reflowable (not fixed format).

For more information, visit Creating Reflowable Books. If you’re using Kindle Create, visit Prepare Reflowable and Print Books with Kindle Create. - have a Kindle Interactive (or NCX) table of contents: Your eBook must include a Kindle Interactive (or NCX) Table of Contents (TOC) to be eligible, as it’s essential for creating audiobook navigation for readers. We recommend using Kindle Create, because it creates an NCX automatically from your manuscript. Visit Create a Table of Contents for more guidance on creating a Kindle Interactive or NCX TOC. If you’re not using Kindle Create, refer to Navigation Guidelines for guidance on creating a Kindle Interactive or NCX TOC. - not have an existing Audible audiobook: An existing Audible audiobook includes:

Audiobooks created through ACX. Audiobooks created (with virtual voice or professional narration) on a previous edition of the eBook. The audiobook on the previous edition must be unpublished before you’ll have the option to create an audiobook with virtual voice on the new edition. Audiobooks created on previously published content. Anthology eBooks that combine content from multiple individual eBooks are not be eligible for a virtual voice audiobook if those individual eBooks already have an associated audiobook. The audiobook would need to be removed from the individual eBook(s) in order to create a virtual voice audiobook for the anthology.

Note: Audiobooks published outside of Audible do not affect eligibility for virtual voice narration. However, if your eBook is enrolled in KDP Select, the KDP Select exclusivity terms apply. - have a supported primary language: Your eBook’s primary language must be set as English, Spanish, Italian, or French before you’ll have the option to create an audiobook with virtual voice.

If your eBook is already published, or has been submitted for publishing, you’ll need to create a new edition of your eBook to be eligible. The new edition should have English, Spanish, Italian, or French as the primary language. For more information, visit Book Titles and Editions.

For the best reader experience, we don’t recommend language excerpts that aren’t in your book’s primary language as they may not be pronounced correctly in the audio. - not be in the public domain: Public domain content is not eligible for audiobooks with virtual voice. - have a cover: To be eligible, your eBook must include a cover. You can use our Cover Creator tool to create an eBook cover in minutes. If you prefer to create your own cover, refer to our eBook cover criteria. - meet eBook cover image criteria: To be eligible, your eBook’s cover must meet our eBook cover criteria. - have a title of less than 200 characters: If your eBook title exceeds 200 characters in length, it is not eligible for an audiobook with virtual voice.

If your eBook is not yet published, you can update the title in your Bookshelf:

Go to your Bookshelf. Next to the eBook, click the ellipsis “…” Select Edit eBook Details. In the Book Title section, update your Title and Subtitle (optional) sections.

If your eBook is already published, or has been submitted for publishing, you’ll need to republish your eBook with a shorter title to be eligible. The new title should have fewer than 200 characters. For more information, visit Create a Book. - have chapters with less than approx. 240k words each: To be eligible, each chapter of your eBook must be approximately 240k words or less. eBooks that exceed the recommended length are not eligible for an audiobook with virtual voice. - have less than 1,001 chapters: To be eligible, your eBook must have 1,000 chapters or less. eBooks that exceed the recommended length are not eligible for an audiobook with virtual voice. - not contain HTML in the title: To be eligible, your eBook’s title cannot include HTML. For more title best practices, visit Book Titles and Editions. - have supported HTML only in the eBook description: eBooks with unsupported HTML tags such as superscript or subscript in the book description are not eligible for an audiobook with virtual voice. - have a primary author or contributor: To be eligible, your eBook requires a Primary Author or Contributor. You can add authors and contributors by updating your book details. - not contain unsupported characters: To be eligible, your eBook can’t include unsupported characters. For example, non-Latin within a word, or Cyrillic characters used to write in languages such as Russian are not supported. You can remove the unsupported characters and republish your eBook.

Format and quality troubleshooting

Audiobooks with virtual voice are currently a beta offering, and there are some known issues, which may change throughout the beta. At this time, we’d like you to understand the following guidance: - Component: Description and impact to listeners: How to avoid or address issue in manuscript - Chapter names/numbers: If chapter names and numbers are formatted as images, listeners may not know when a new chapter begins.: Format chapter names and numbers as text in your eBook manuscript rather than images. - Footnotes: Numbers or references may be narrated where they are encountered in the text and may interrupt the flow.: Format Footnotes as superscripts/subscripts so they are not included in the narration. - HTML/code excerpts: Any sections of HTML or other code may result in unintelligible narration for listeners.: Consider appropriateness for audiobook. - Image captions: If you have images with captions in your eBook, the captions may be included in the narration, but the image may be excluded.: Ensure that text captions make sense to listeners who will not be able to see the image. - Non-primary language excerpts: Any language excerpts that are not in the book’s primary language may not be pronounced correctly in the audio.: While you can edit one or two words or short phrases phonetically, longer passages are not recommended at this time. - Numbers: When two formats are presented, both formats may be narrated. For example, “a six (6) by nine (9) book.”: Consider impact to listeners when many numbers in multiple formats are present. - Tables: Tables are narrated row by row (from left to right), which may be hard for listeners to follow.: Consider appropriateness of long tables for the audiobook format.

Edit audio in the Virtual Voice Studio

Edit audio in the Virtual Voice Studio

The Virtual Voice Studio (VVS) is where you can preview and edit the audio, and hear what your audiobook will sound like to listeners. There are multiple ways you can edit the audio outlined on this page. We recommend using the latest versions of Firefox or Chrome on a desktop computer for the best experience using Virtual Voice Studio. ##### Contents - Before you start - Add a pause - Change voice speed - Edit pronunciation - Set start reading location - Follow playing audio

Before you start

Note that you can search your manuscript using the search bar at the top of your manuscript. You can also navigate the chapters of your audiobook using the table of contents on the left. Please be aware that the Clear All button will reset your audio removing any pauses, changes to voice speed, or edits to pronunciation. Note: audiobooks with virtual voice: - are created from the start reading location (SRL) to the end reading location (ERL). For example, the table of contents is before the SRL, so it will not be included in the audiobook. - are created only from the text. Any images (including image representations of the text), graphs, or tables are not included. - add a pause between each paragraph or new line in the eBook. Pauses between paragraphs or new lines can’t be removed. - don’t have the functionality to skip image or graph captions at this time.

Add a pause

  1. Select the space before or after a word or character where you would like to insert the pause.

  2. Select the arrow next to Pause to expand the section.

  3. Choose Short, Medium, or Long from the drop-down menu.

  4. Select the Add pause button.

  5. An indicator will appear where you added the pause specifying its length.

  6. Select the pause tag in your script that’s labelled either, Short, Medium, or Long.

  7. In the Pause section, choose the desired pause length from the drop-down menu.

  8. Select the Apply button and the pause length will update.

Change voice speed
  1. Select the word you want to speed up or slow down.
  2. Select the arrow next to Voice speed to expand the section.
  3. Choose your desired speed from the drop-down menu.
  4. Select the Apply button.
Edit pronunciation

  1. Select the word you’d like to edit so it’s highlighted.

  2. Select the Edit pronunciation button from either the Quick actions menu or the editing tools on the right. The Pronunciation pop-up window will open.

  3. Spell out the words using plain language or how the word sounds in the How it should be said field. You can use the play buttons to listen to the existing and new pronunciation. Spelling examples: for “Edinburgh,” the spelling could be “ed-in-bruh” or “ed-in-bur-uh”; for “lead,” the spelling could be “leed” or “led”.

  4. If you want all instances of the word to be pronounced the same way, check Apply to all instances.Note: If you check this option, it will apply to all instances of the word that exist today and any that are added in the future.

  5. Select the Apply pronunciation button.

  6. Select the word you previously edited, and select the Remove button on the right under Pronunciation

  7. A confirmation pop-up will open. Select Remove to revert the pronunciation back to the original.

  • Component: Potential pronunciation issues: How to change pronunciation in Virtual Voice Studio
  • Abbreviations: May not be pronounced in the intended way: Write the word in full. For example, “corporation” instead of “corp.”
  • Acronyms: Acronyms may be accidentally pronounced as a word instead of individual letters.: Write the term in full or each letter phonetically. For example, “United States” or “you ess” instead of “US”
  • Dates: Dates might be pronounced incorrectly: Write the date by spelling out the month, day, and year. For example, “January first two thousand twenty four”
  • Ellipse: An ellipse may not signify a pause in narration: Insert a pause at the location of the ellipse
  • Fractions: Some fractions may be read incorrectly: Spell out the fraction instead of using numerals. For example, “one quarter” instead of “1/4”
  • Homographs: Words that are spelled the same but are pronounced differently may be pronounced incorrectly. For example, “live”: Write the word phonetically. For example, “liv” for the verb “live”
  • Measurement symbols: Feet and inches symbols may be narrated incorrectly or excluded: Replace the symbol with the word “feet” or “inches”. We do not recommend selecting Apply to all instances
  • Onomatopoeia: Words representing sounds may not be narrated as intended.: Edit the pronunciation by writing the sound phonetically
  • Punctuation: Some punctuation may be inappropriately narrated. For example, “slash”: Select the word, phrase, or punctuation, and enter the correct pronunciation in the How it should be said field.  

Punctuation at the start or end of the word: punctuation is included as part of the word selection. You can delete it from the How it’s spelled field to edit the pronunciation, regardless of the punctuation. Or you can leave the punctuation, if you are adding specific pronunciation for the words containing that specific punctuation. Individual punctuation: any punctuation with space on either side can be selected on its own to edit pronunciation. Punctuation between two words or numbers: the punctuation is included as part of the word selection. For example, “1/2” could be edited to: “one slash two,” “half,” “one of two,” or “January second.” - Roman numerals: May not be recognized as numbers: Spell out the number (“one”). We do not recommend selecting Apply to all instances

Set start reading location
  1. Open the Virtual Voice Studio.
  2. Under Editing Tools on the right, click Reading Locations.
  3. Select a word or space in your text.
  4. Under Quick Actions, click Add Start Reading Location.
Follow playing audio

Getting started with audiobooks with virtual voice

Getting started with audiobooks with virtual voice

An audiobook with virtual voice is a KDP beta offering that uses computer-generated speech technology. As a KDP beta participant, you can create audiobooks from eligible eBooks on your KDP Bookshelf with virtual voice for free at this time. ##### Contents - Eligibility - Before you start - Create an audiobook with virtual voice - Listen to and choose a virtual voice - Update your eBook and/or audiobook - Promote your audiobook

Eligibility

To be eligible for an audiobook with virtual voice, your eBook must meet the required criteria. Learn more about eligibility and troubleshooting. Note: We reserve the right to determine the types of eBooks that we accept in the beta program. We may choose not to accept your eBook for creation of an audiobook or to remove your audiobook from sale at any time. ##### Before you start - Table of contents: a Kindle Interactive (or NCX) table of contents is required to build your audiobook. Please ensure your table of contents is complete, in the correct order, and doesn’t use images for text. Also make sure that all content in your book is contained within a chapter. - Typos: check spelling and grammar, and complete a proofread of your manuscript. - Chapter names/numbers: ensure chapter names/numbers are formatted as text (rather than images) or they will not be read to indicate where your listener is in the audiobook. - Footnotes: ensure footnotes are formatted as superscripts/subscripts so that they’re not included as part of the audiobook’s content.

Create an audiobook with virtual voice
  1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf, and select Add Audible audiobook with virtual voice next to the eligible eBook. It may take up to 15 seconds for your eBook info to process and the audiobook setup page to open.
  2. On the audiobook setup page, you can choose a book voice from the available options. Audio samples are available to help you decide. You can filter the virtual voices by attributes (e.g., age range). If you don’t select a voice, we’ll assign a default voice. Note: you can change the selected virtual voice after publishing.
  3. Enter your list price between $3.99 and $14.99. Learn more about audiobook pricing and royalties.
  4. After your audio file is ready, you can preview and edit the narration by selecting Open Virtual Voice Studio, which will open in the same window.
  5. When you’ve finished previewing/editing your audio file, select Return to audiobook setup from the top-right corner.
  6. Back on the audiobook setup page, select Publish audiobook.

Note that it can take up to 72 hours for your audiobook to appear in the Amazon Store or on Audible, and both your eBook and audiobook will be locked for editing until the audiobook is live. Important: Your audiobook will be held to the same content quality guidelines as your eBook. ##### Listen to and choose a virtual voice Visit the virtual voice audio samples page to listen to all virtual voice options. You can also listen to samples from the audiobook setup page. After creating an audiobook from your eligible eBook, you can listen to your audiobook, and choose your book’s virtual voice by following the steps below. Select or change your audiobook’s virtual voice 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf, and select Continue setup next to the audiobook you want to edit. 2. On the audiobook setup page, select the virtual voice option. You can listen to the voices using the Play sample link. 3. After you’ve chosen a virtual voice, select Publish audiobook. Any edits you previously made in the Virtual Voice Studio will be transferred to the new virtual voice.

Listen to your audiobook or choose a different virtual voice by chapter 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf, and select Continue setup next to the audiobook you want to edit. 2. On the audiobook setup page, click Open Virtual Voice Studio. 3. In Virtual Voice Studio, select Change voice from the menu at the top of the screen. A popup window will open where you can play samples and select a new book voice to Apply.

To choose different voices for each chapter, select the chapter you want to update, and click Choose Chapter Voice. 4. After selecting a voice, click Apply to this chapter.

Note: The book voice will be used for any chapter where you don’t apply a chapter voice. You can update the book voice on the audiobook setup page or in the Virtual Voice Studio. Your book voice updates won’t change any of your chapter voice selections. ##### Update your eBook and/or audiobook There are three types of changes you can make directly in your audiobook setup without updating your eBook: edit your list price, select a different virtual voice, or modify the audio. If required, you will be prompted to set your start reading location (SRL) before you publish your audiobook. Note: All audiobook updates can take up to 72 hours to appear in the Amazon Store or on Audible, and both your eBook and audiobook will be locked for editing until the audiobook is live. Edit your list price 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf, and select Continue setup next to the audiobook you want to edit. 2. On the audiobook setup page, under Pricing and royalties, enter your audiobook list price. 3. Select Publish audiobook.

Learn more about audiobook pricing and royalties Select a different virtual voice 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf, and select Continue setup next to the audiobook you want to edit. 2. On the audiobook setup page, select the virtual voice option. You can listen to the voices using the Play sample link. 3. After you’ve chosen a virtual voice, select Publish audiobook.

Edit pauses, voice speed, and pronunciation 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf, and select Continue setup next to the audiobook you want to edit. 2. On the audiobook setup page, select Open Virtual Voice Studio. Learn how to edit narration including pauses, pronunciation, and voice speed. 3. When you’re finished editing your audio, select Return to audiobook setup. 4. Back on the audiobook setup page, select Publish audiobook.

If you have feedback on the audiobook setup or Virtual Voice Studio, please complete our survey. The survey is hosted by Qualtrics, so you’ll visit their site to fill it out. For specific guidelines on pronunciation, see the Virtual Voice Studio pronunciation guide. ##### Promote your audiobook During the beta, you can promote your published audiobooks on social media and through author newsletters as you would other published titles. However, please note that the following promotion products/features are not available at this time: - A+ Content - Amazon Ads - KDP Select promotions - Pre-orders

Please keep in mind, the author experience for the audiobook beta is confidential under the KDP Terms and Conditions

Pricing, royalties, and reports for audiobooks

List price

Royalties
Purchase and listening types
  • Transaction type: Description: Payment schedule
  • Audiobook Sales – ALC (ALC = a la carte): A non-Audible member purchases your audiobook. The price at which we sell your audiobook may not be the same as your List Price.: Monthly
  • Audiobook Sales – Add-on: A customer purchases your audiobook on Amazon at a discounted price at the same time or after they purchase or borrow your eBook.: Monthly
  • Audiobook Sales – AL (AL = Audible listener): An Audible member uses an Audible credit to purchase your audiobook or an Amazon Music Unlimited member or Audible Standard Plan member listens to your audiobook for their monthly audiobook selection.: Monthly
  • Audiobook Sales – ALOP (Audible listener over plan): An Audible member purchases your audiobook at an exclusive member discount on your set list price.: Monthly
  • Audible subscription royalties: An Audible member listens to your audiobook on Audible Plus as part of their membership.: Monthly
KDP Reports
  • Report: Where to find audiobook details
  • Dashboard: Audiobook orders, royalties, and KENP are included in your dashboard totals and your download.
  • Orders: Processed audiobook orders for both Amazon and Audible will display under Retail sales. Includes standalone, add-on, and credit orders and Amazon Music Unlimited monthly audiobook selections.
  • KENP: Includes combined pages listened to on Audible Plus and pages read from Kindle Unlimited (KU).

Note: Although pages listened to and read are combined in reporting, payments for these activities come from separate funds. - Promotions: Not available for audiobook - Pre-orders: Not available for audiobook - Month-to-Date: Audiobook unit and subscription transactions are added. Filter by Audiobook in the format filter. - Prior Month’s Royalties: Check the Audiobook royalties column for standalone, add-on, ALOP, and credit purchases and Amazon Music Unlimited monthly audiobook selections. Check the KENP column for royalties earned based on pages listened/read via subscription programs. - Royalties Estimator: Check the Audiobook royalties column for standalone, add-on, and ALOP. See KENP column for royalties earned based on pages listened/read via subscription programs. Note: credit purchases are paid out monthly and are not estimated. - Payments: Payment Source for standalone, add-on, ALOP, and credit purchases is shown as Audiobook Sales and/or Subscription Royalties for KENP reads and listens.

KDP Select

Your audiobook’s KDP Select enrollment status is determined by the eBook of the same title. If your eBook is enrolled in KDP Select, the associated audiobook with virtual voice will also be enrolled in KDP Select and only your eBook will remain available through Kindle Unlimited. Your audiobook will also be included in the unlimited listening catalog available to Audible Plus and Premium Plus subscribers. Earnings for each subscription program are based on a number of factors, such as customer reading behavior and subscription pricing. As a result, the payout rate for pages listened to from Audible’s subscriptions may differ from what your eBook earns for pages read in Kindle Unlimited (KU). The audiobooks with virtual voice beta will not impact the funds available for qualified reads of eBooks. Audiobooks with virtual voice listening activity from Audible Plus is paid for from a separate fund that is in addition to the fund amount paid for Kindle Unlimited eBook reading activity. As with eBooks, audiobooks enrolled in KDP Select must be exclusive to Audible for the KDP Select enrollment period. This requirement applies to any audio edition of that book. If the audiobook with virtual voice is unpublished, exclusivity will still be required through the remainder of the current 90-day period of participation in KDP Select. Note: Audiobooks with virtual voice are not currently eligible for Free Book Promotions and Kindle Countdown Deals (KCD).

Terms and Conditions for the Beta Version of Audiobooks with Virtual Voice

Terms and Conditions for the Beta Version of Audiobooks with Virtual Voice

Terms and Conditions for the Beta Version of Audiobooks with Virtual Voice

  1. Eligibility. In order to offer an AVV Edition, the following requirements must be met for the corresponding Digital Book: you must hold the associated audio rights, it must be in English and currently offered for sale, and it must not consist primarily of content in the public domain. We reserve the right to determine the types of Digital Books that we accept in the AVV Program. We may choose not to accept your Digital Book for creation of an AVV Edition or to remove your AVV Edition from sale at any time.
  2. Grant of Rights. In addition to the Grant of Rights in Section 5.5 of the Agreement, you grant to each Amazon party, throughout the term of the Agreement, a nonexclusive, irrevocable, right and license to create AVV Editions and make available all or any portion of AVV Editions though Amazon Properties for customers to listen to online and offline, including on portable devices. Subject to the authorizations you grant us under this Agreement, as between you and us, you retain all ownership rights in and to the copyrights and all other rights and interest in and to your Books, and we retain ownership in the AVV Edition file.
  3. Pricing and Royalties. To be accepted in the Program, AVV Editions must have a List Price between $3.99-14.99 USD. If you are not in breach of your obligations under this Agreement, for each AVV Edition sold to a customer through the Program, the Amazon party that made the sale (or whose affiliate made the sale) will pay you a Royalty as follows: (a) 40% of all A La Carte Net Sales Receipts (as defined below) or (b) 40% of all Membership Net Sales Receipts (as defined below) for each individual sale of an AVV Edition to a customer who is a member of one of Audible’s membership programs during the immediately preceding monthly period. “A La Carte Sales” means a cash sale of an AVV Edition. “A La Carte Net Sales Receipts” means the monetary amount received by Amazon from a la carte sales of each AVV Edition, less any cash incentives, promotional discounts, sales or use taxes, excise taxes, value-added taxes, duties, exchanges and returns.
  4. “Membership Sale” means non-cash sales of AVV Editions to a members or prospective member of one of Audible’s membership programs (excluding returns). “Membership Net Sales Receipts” means, for each Membership Sale, the monetary amount obtained by multiplying the AudibleListener Allocation Factor by Audible’s a la carte price for the AVV Edition at the time the AudibleListener Allocation Factor is calculated.
  5. The “AudibleListener Allocation Factor” means the total of all Membership Sales receipts derived from sales of all content sold by Audible in the applicable accounting period, less any cash incentives, promotional discounts, device subsidies or rebates, sales or use taxes, excise taxes, value-added taxes, duties and returns, divided by the total a la carte value (as determined by Audible’s applicable a la carte price for the AVV Edition at the time the AudibleListener Allocation Factor is calculated) of the membership sales of all content sold by Audible in the applicable accounting period.
  6. KDP Select and Subscription Programs. If the Digital Book for your AVV Edition is enrolled in KDP Select, your AVV Edition may also be made available to listeners through the Audible Plus catalog or a similar subscription service. When you include a Digital Book in KDP Select, you also give us the exclusive right to sell and distribute the corresponding AVV Edition. During your Digital Book’s 90-day period of exclusivity, you also cannot sell or distribute, or give anyone else the right to sell or distribute, your Book in audio format. AVV Editions of Digital Books included in KDP Select will be automatically included in Audible Plus or similar subscription service. For AVV Editions, you will be eligible to earn a share of a fund on a monthly basis for customers listening to your AVV Edition via Audible Plus or a similar subscription service. You will earn a share of the monthly fund based on the amount of your content listened to by customers. These shares are your total Royalty for customer access to your AVV Edition through the Audible Plus catalog or similar subscription service. We will set the criteria for determining how much of your content is listened to and how to determine the proportionate allocation of the fund. We may publicly announce the top AVV Editions, including the author, publisher, number of qualified listens, and subscription royalties earned.
  7. Updates and Improvements. We reserve the right to add, remove, refine, or modify the voices available for or applied to AVV Editions. Information and material you provide may be used to improve our products and services.
  8. Amendment. We reserve the right to change the Terms and Conditions for the Beta Version of Audiobooks with Virtual Voice at any time. We will give you notice of changes to these beta terms by posting new terms in place of the old at https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/GWHSFAK69P2537YR with a revision date indicated at the top or by sending an email to the email address then registered for your Program account.
  9. Inapplicable Terms. The following sections of the Agreement do not apply to the Audiobooks with Virtual Voice Program: 5.2.3 Lending Kindle Books, 5.3.2 Currency Conversion, 5.3.3 Multiple List Prices, 5.4.1 Royalties, 5.4.3 Payment Currencies, 5.4.4 Payment Terms for Brazilian Publishers, Terms and Conditions for KDP Select Program, Terms and Conditions for KDP Pre-Orders, the Digital Book Pricing Page and the Print Book Pricing Page.

KDP Publishing: Beta: Kindle Translate

Getting Started with Kindle Translate

Getting Started with Kindle Translate

Kindle Translate is Amazon’s new AI-powered translation service that enables authors to translate their eBooks between multiple language options. As a KDP beta participant, you can create translations from eligible eBooks on your KDP Bookshelf. ##### Contents - Eligibility - Create and publish translations - Automatically translate and publish in new languages - Preview translations - Update translations - Change cover - Edit list price - Edit KDP Select enrollment

Eligibility

To be eligible to use Kindle Translate to create translations, your eBook must meet the required criteria. Learn more about eligibility and troubleshooting. Note: We reserve the right to determine the types of eBooks that we accept in the beta program. We may choose not to accept your eBook for the creation of translations or to remove your translations from sale at any time. ##### Create and publish translations To create a translation: 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf. 2. Select Translate your eBook next to the eligible eBook. 3. On the Kindle Translate page, choose the languages you would like to translate your eBook into. 4. Choose your KDP Select enrollment, territorial rights, and pricing. Optionally, change your cover. 5. Select Submit for publishing.

Note: Translations can take a few hours to be created (up to 24 hours). When you create a new translation, you can: - Submit for publishing any time during the translation process. We’ll notify you when the translations are live. It can take up to 72 hours for translations to appear in the Amazon store and your source eBook will be locked for editing until translations are live. - Start the translation process and complete translation set up. When translations are created, you can return to your translation set up page to preview translations before you publish.

Important: Translations are held to the same content quality guidelines as your eBook. ##### Automatically translate and publish in new languages When you set up translations for eligible eBooks, you can enable translations to be automatically translated and published into new languages as they become available for Kindle Translate. To view available language pairing options, visit Kindle Translate Languages. Please note that If you already have a translation available in a language that later becomes available for Kindle Translate, enabling this setting may result in the creation of duplicate translations. For an optimal customer experience, only one translated edition per language can be available in the Kindle Store. If enabling this setting results in a duplicate translation, you can review and choose which one you prefer to make available in the Kindle Store. Important: You must have worldwide distribution rights to enable the option. If you don’t have worldwide rights, you can translate each supported language and select individual territory rights from the translation set up page. To enable automatic translation and publication: 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf. 2. Select Manage translations or Continue setup next to the Kindle Translate book. 3. On the Kindle Translate Management page, select Adjust translations settings. 4. Under Languages, turn on Automatically translate and publish in new languages. 5. Select Submit for publishing to confirm selection.

When you enable automatic translations: - Eligible eBooks will automatically translate and publish as new languages become available. - Translated editions will use the default cover. The default cover displays your existing cover image with a white border and the language at the top. You can change your cover at any time. - We’ll use your source eBook’s list price and royalty plan for all translated editions by default. If you set a different list price in your Kindle Translate Pricing and Royalties settings, we’ll use that price for each translated edition. You can edit your list price for your translations at any time. Learn more about Kindle Translate pricing and royalties.

To disable automatic translations and publication, follow the above steps and turn off the Automatically translate and publish in new languages setting. ##### Preview translations After your translation is complete, you can preview the translations. 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf. 2. Under the Kindle eBook title, click Continue set up next to the Kindle Translate book. 3. On the Languages section, click the language preview under the Preview column. 4. Select Submit for publishing when ready to publish translations.

  1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf.
  2. Under the Kindle eBook title, click Manage translations next to the Kindle Translate book.
  3. On the Kindle Translate Management page, select Adjust translation settings.
  4. Go to the Languages section and click the language preview under the Preview column.

Within the preview, you can see the translated content and the cover. You’ll see that the primary text and supplementary materials such as the copyright notice page has been translated. ###### Cover preview - If you choose to publish with the default cover, the preview displays your existing cover design with a white border and the translated language edition at the top. - If you choose to upload your own cover, the preview displays your uploaded custom cover.

Note: Occasionally, if a book doesn’t meet Amazon’s 7-step quality assurance threshold, translations won’t be available for you to preview and publish. To learn more about our quality assurance threshold, visit Kindle Translate Quality. ##### Update translations You can edit your list price, your KDP Select enrollment, and change your cover in Kindle Translate without updating your source eBook. Note: Updates can take up to 72 hours to appear in the Amazon Store. Both your eBook and translations will be locked for editing until the changes are live. ###### Change cover When you submit translations for publishing, the default cover is used, unless you upload your own cover. The default cover displays your existing cover image with a white border and the language edition at the top. To change your cover: 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf. 2. Select Manage translations next to the translation you want to edit. 3. On the Kindle Translate Management page, select Adjust translation settings. 4. Scroll to the Covers section and select Change covers. 5. Choose the Upload cover and select a JPG or TIFF file. 6. Save your changes to return to the Kindle Translate Management page. 7. Select Submit for publishing.

Learn more about cover image guidelines. ###### Edit list price To edit your list price: 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf. 2. Select Manage translations next to the translation you want to edit. 3. On the Kindle Translate Management page, under Pricing and royalties, enter your list price. 4. Select Submit for publishing.

Learn more about Kindle Translate pricing and royalties. ###### Edit KDP Select enrollment To edit your KDP Select enrollment: 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf. 2. Select Manage translations next to the translation you want to edit. 3. On the Kindle Translate Management page, select KDP Select info. 4. Update your KDP Select enrollment and select Submit for publishing.

Learn more about KDP Select. ##### Book detail updates Translations are created from your source eBook using its existing book details and translating them, such as the title and author name. These book details (also called metadata) cannot be changed on translations independently of the source eBook. To update your book details, edit your source eBook. You will then be prompted to apply the same updates to the translations after publishing updates to your source eBook. Note:* If you make changes to your book title, we’ll automatically update your translations. If you uploaded your own cover for translated editions, we recommend reviewing your covers after your source eBook is published to ensure they match the new title. To change your cover, follow the instructions above.* ###### Manuscript edits If you publish updates to your eBook manuscript, you’ll be prompted to also re-translate and publish the updated translations. ##### Manage series translations Kindle Translate automatically creates the series for you within 5 business days after your translated titles go live. You can verify series creation by checking your books in the Amazon store. Occasionally, if a book within a series doesn’t meet Amazon’s 7-step quality assurance threshold, translations won’t be available for you to preview and publish. This may result in an incomplete series. We understand that an incomplete series can impact readers’ experience. To manage incomplete series translations, you can consider the below options: - Unpublish translations for the entire series - Unpublish translations for specific titles within the series - Explore alternative translation options, such as engaging professional translators

We’re working to continuously improve our translation service during the Kindle Translate beta. When we make improvements, we automatically retranslate any Kindle Translate eBook that previously didn’t meet our quality standards resulting in a “Cannot be published” status. You’ll be notified when an improved translation is available for publishing. To learn more about our quality assurance threshold, visit Kindle Translate Quality. ###### Combine translation types in a series Creating or editing your series to combine Kindle Translate eBooks with other translated eBooks is not available through the KDP Bookshelf. Contact us to create or update your series to combine translation types. Your eBooks must meet these requirements before adding them to a series: - The primary contributor or series title match with the existing series. - The series information is included in the cover, manuscript, and/or description of the book. - The translated book is in the same language.

  • After we combine different translation types, you can no longer edit the series from your KDP Bookshelf. Contact us for any future changes.
  • Custom descriptions are not available for series with multiple authors. We’ll display the description from the first book in the series.
Unpublish translations

You can unpublish translations from the Kindle Translate Management page, independent of your source eBook. If you unpublish your source eBook, the associated Kindle Translate eBook will also be unpublished. It takes up to 72 hours for the books to be unpublished. To unpublish a translation: 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf 2. Search for your source eBook title in your Bookshelf 3. Under the Kindle eBook title, click Manage translations next to the Kindle Translate book. You’ll be redirected to the Kindle Translate Management page. 4. Select Manage eBook next to the Kindle Translate eBook you want to unpublish 5. Choose Unpublish translation from the dropdown options 6. Confirm the title and ASIN to unpublish in the confirmation window

If your translation is enrolled in KDP Select and you unpublish it, the book will be removed from Kindle Unlimited. However, you must continue to comply with KDP Select exclusivity requirements through the remainder of the current 90-day enrollment period. ##### Promote and advertise your translations During the beta, you can promote your published translations in the same ways you promote original language eBooks, including social media and through author newsletters as you would other published titles. After your book is available in a new marketplace, you can reach new readers with Amazon Ads. Get started with these resources: - Sponsored Products: New to advertising? Start with the author’s guide to Sponsored Products. This is a great resource to review whether you’re advertising at home or in a new marketplace. - Explore Amazon Ads’ international advertising features and tools: A complete guide to features and tools designed to help you advertise effectively across countries. Discover keyword localization and targeting, Amazon Ads translations, and the multi-country Sponsored Ads campaign manager. - Set up your first Sponsored Products campaign in a new country: A step-by-step video tutorial shows you how to create and manage campaigns across multiple countries in just a few clicks from one dashboard, set country-specific budgets and bids in local currencies, and monitor performance metrics globally or by country.

Please keep in mind, details of the author experience for the Kindle Translate beta are subject to your confidentiality obligations under the KDP Terms and Conditions. Please don’t share or discuss any specifics or take screenshots of the Kindle Translate beta experience.

Kindle Translate Eligibility and Troubleshooting

Kindle Translate Eligibility and Troubleshooting

To be eligible to create a translation using Kindle Translate, your eBook must meet the required criteria. ##### Contents - Checking eligibility - Eligibility criteria and troubleshooting - Format and quality troubleshooting

Checking eligibility

After your eBook is Live, we will complete an eligibility check against the criteria below. If your eBook is eligible, the option to Translate your eBook will appear in your KDP Bookshelf. If you would like to translate an eBook that’s ineligible, you can review the eligibility criteria and publish updates to the source eBook. The link to create a translation should appear on your Bookshelf after the updated eBook is Live and passes the eligibility check. Note: We reserve the right to determine the types of eBooks that we accept in the beta program. We may choose not to accept your eBook for creation of a translation or to remove your translation from sale at any time. ##### Eligibility criteria and troubleshooting Review requirements for your eBook to be eligible to create a translation using Kindle Translate and potential troubleshooting steps below. If your eBook is ineligible, check the reason(s) listed by selecting Why isn’t my eBook eligible? on your KDP Bookshelf. - Your eBook must: How to correct - have a Live status: Your eBook must be Live before you will have the option to create a translation. Your eBook’s status cannot be Publishing. Note that eBooks available for pre-order are not eligible. For more information on publishing timelines, visit Book Status. - be reflowable (not a fixed format): For more information, visit Creating Reflowable Books. If you’re using Kindle Create, visit Prepare Reflowable and Print Books with Kindle Create. - have a supported primary language: Your eBook’s primary language must be set as English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, or Spanish before you’ll have the option to create translations using Kindle Translate.

For the best reader experience, we don’t recommend language excerpts that differ from your eBook’s primary language as they may not be translated correctly. To view available translation options, visit Kindle Translate Languages. - not be a preorder: To be eligible, your eBook’s title cannot be a preorder. - not be in the public domain: Public domain content is not eligible for Kindle Translate. This applies to books that primarily consist of public domain material, even where that material has been translated, annotated, or illustrated. - not be books that are already translations: Books that are already translations are not eligible for Kindle Translate. Kindle Translate works best from original source-language content to ensure the highest quality output.

If your book’s original language is not yet supported, we are actively expanding our language coverage and will notify authors when additional languages become available. - have a cover: To be eligible, your eBook must include a cover. You can use our Cover Creator tool to create an eBook cover in minutes. If you prefer to create your own cover, refer to our eBook cover criteria. - have a primary author or contributor: To be eligible, your eBook requires a Primary Author or Contributor. You can add authors and contributors by updating your book details. - be suitable for translation: Consider the types of books that are best suited for translation. Your eBook must not be empty or have empty chapters. Books with a lot of images, contain multiple languages, have tables, graphs, or code excerpts may not provide the best reader experience due to the current limitations of the Kindle Translate service (for example, a cookbook or comic book). - complete post-publishing processing: We’re preparing your eBook for translations. This process can take up to 72 hours.

If you still see this message for more than 72 hours, contact us for assistance.

Format and quality troubleshooting

Kindle Translate is currently a beta offering and we’re working to improve the service over time. Due to limitations of our service, there are certain types of content that achieve the best translation results. Please consider the following. ###### Content that translates well: - Fiction works (novels, short stories, narrative non-fiction) - Business books and self-help guides - Straightforward instructional content - Standard prose and dialogue

Content that may not translate well:
  • Highly technical or specialized terminology
  • Complex literary devices and wordplay
  • Poetry and creative works with intricate language
  • Content with extensive cultural references
  • Books with complex formatting or structure
Elements that can’t be translated:
  • Text embedded in images, charts, or graphics
  • Complex infographics and data visualizations
  • Language excerpts that aren’t in your book’s primary language
  • Book subtitles

Kindle Translate Languages

Kindle Translate Languages

You can use Kindle Translate to create translations into the supported languages listed below for your eligible eBooks. When setting up a translation, you can also enable automatic translation and publication as new languages become available. For an optimal reader experience, we don’t recommend language excerpts that are different from your eBook’s primary language. These excerpts may not translate correctly. Learn more about Kindle Translate Eligibility and Troubleshooting. ##### Contents - Supported languages

Supported languages

  • Source eBook language →: Can be translated into

  • English: French (France), German, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish (Spain)

  • French: English (US)

  • German

  • Italian

  • Portuguese

  • Spanish

  • When you translate into English, the default translation language is English (US).

  • This page is regularly updated as new translation options are added.

Kindle Translate Quality

Kindle Translate Quality

Translations created using Kindle Translate are held to the high standards customers have come to expect from Amazon. Translations become available to preview and publish only if they meet Amazon’s 7-step quality assurance threshold. This threshold evaluates fidelity to the original work, writing style, and idiomatic expressions. It also assesses other literary elements specific to long-form book translation. We check that we can create a fully formatted translation from the source eBook before evaluating the translation quality. If your eBook isn’t eligible for translation, it may not meet certain formatting or content requirements. Visit our eligibility criteria page for more details. ##### Contents - Quality standards - Translation quality outcomes - Translation quality improvements

Quality standards

We evaluate the translation quality based on the number and type of errors. We won’t make translations available to preview and publish if they contain many errors or significant ones such as mistranslations. ###### Quality checks include: ###### Content accuracy - Mistranslations - Idiomatic expressions - Named entities (proper nouns, titles) - Additions or omissions of content

Language usage
  • Terminology consistency
  • Form of address (formal/informal)
  • Gender consistency in character references
Technical Elements
  • Grammar
  • Spelling
Translation quality outcomes

After evaluating translation quality, we’ll update the translation status. This lets you know if the translation is ready for you to preview and publish. The possible translation outcomes are as follows: - Status: Translation: Quality Check: Action required - Ready to publish: Complete: Passed: You can proceed to preview and publish translations. - Cannot be published: Complete: Didn’t pass: No action is needed. We couldn’t create a translation that meets our quality standards due to current technology limitations.

Note: If you selected Submit for publishing during the translation process, we’ll notify you when your translations are live. ##### Translation quality improvements We’re working to continuously improve our translation service during the Kindle Translate beta. When we make improvements to our service, we automatically retranslate any Kindle Translate eBook that previously didn’t meet our quality standards resulting in a “Cannot be published” status. Each retranslation goes through our rigorous quality evaluation before it is made available for publishing. You’ll be notified when an improved translation is available for publishing. As a beta participant, you can complete our feedback survey on Kindle Translate to share further insights with the beta team.

Pricing, royalties, and reports for translations

Pricing, royalties, and reports for translations

Contents
  • Pricing and royalties
  • KDP Reports
  • KDP Select
Pricing and royalties

You can choose to apply your source eBook’s royalty plan and list price to your translations or select new royalty plans and list prices. As a reminder, we offer two royalty plans for eBooks: - 35% royalty - 70% royalty*

To see the minimum and maximum list price for each royalty plan, check our list price requirements. *Sales to customers outside of the 70% eligible territories will receive 35% of the list price. Learn more about eBook royalty options. ##### KDP Reports As a beta participant, you can view your translated eBook orders, royalties, and payments in KDP Reports as you would any other eBook. Learn more about KDP Reports. ##### KDP Select You can manage your KDP Select enrollment separately for translation(s) without impacting your source eBook’s enrollment. If your source eBook is enrolled in KDP Select when you submit its translations for publication, those translations will also be enrolled in KDP Select for 90 days. If your source eBook isn’t enrolled, you can choose to enroll your translations to reach more readers. This enrollment will automatically renew for additional 90-day periods, unless you opt out from the Kindle Translate management page. ###### To edit your KDP Select enrollment: 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf. 2. Select Manage translations next to the translation you want to edit. 3. On the Kindle Translate management page, select KDP Select info. 4. Update your KDP Select enrollment and select Submit for publishing.

Learn more about KDP Select.

Terms and Conditions for the Beta Version of Kindle Translate

Terms and Conditions for the Beta Version of Kindle Translate

  1. Kindle Translate Program. The Kindle Translate Program enables you to create translated editions of your Digital Books using our Kindle Translate service (each such translated edition, a “Kindle Translate Edition”) and make Kindle Translate Editions available to Amazon customers. The Kindle Translate Program constitutes part of the Program, and Kindle Translate Editions constitute “Digital Books” and “Books” under the KDP Terms.
  2. Eligibility. In order to offer a Kindle Translate Edition, the Digital Book being translated must meet the following requirements: (i) it must be currently offered for sale in a language eligible for translation via the Kindle Translate Program, (ii) it must not consist primarily of content in the public domain, (iii) it must be a Digital book for which you hold the applicable translation rights, and (iv) it must not itself be a Kindle Translate Edition. We reserve the right to determine which Digital Books we accept into the Kindle Translate Program, and accordingly we may choose not to allow creation of a Kindle Translate Edition for your Digital Book or to remove your Kindle Translate Edition from sale at any time. We may decline to offer a Kindle Translate Edition if we are unable to create a translation that meets our quality standards.
  3. Grant of Rights. Solely with respect to Kindle Translate Editions, the print and distribution rights you grant to Amazon under Section 5.5 of the KDP Terms are and will remain exclusive to the Amazon parties. You additionally grant to each Amazon party a nonexclusive, irrevocable, right and license to translate each Digital Book you submit to the Kindle Translate Program. Amazon retains ownership of Kindle Translate Edition files, and you may not sell or distribute Kindle Translate Editions outside of the Program. Unless your Kindle Translate Edition is enrolled in KDP Select and subject to the exclusivity right granted to Amazon pursuant to Section 1 of the Terms and Conditions for KDP Select Program (the “KDP Select Terms”) contained within the KDP Terms, you may create alternative translations of your Digital Book in the same language as the Kindle Translate Edition and distribute those alternative translations outside of the Program.
  4. KDP Select Enrollment. If a Digital Book is enrolled in KDP Select when you submit a Kindle Translate Edition of the Digital Book for self-publishing, Amazon may enroll the Kindle Translate Edition in KDP Select. This enrollment will last for a period of 90 days starting from the date of publication and will automatically renew for additional 90-day periods, unless you opt out through the KDP website before renewal. Kindle Translate Editions that are included in KDP Select are subject to the KDP Select Terms, including the exclusivity right granted to Amazon.
  5. Updates and Improvements. We reserve the right to add, remove, refine, or modify the features and functionality available through the Kindle Translate Program. Information and material you provide may be used to improve our products and services.
  6. Amendment. We reserve the right to change the Kindle Translate Terms at any time. We will give you notice of changes by posting new terms in place of the old at https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G3QW74S97633MNF6 with a revision date indicated at the top or by sending an email to the email address then registered for your Program account. Except to the extent modified by these Kindle Translate Terms with respect to the Kindle Translate Program and Kindle Translate Editions, all terms in the KDP Terms remain unchanged and in full force and effect.

KDP Publishing: Create a Book

Accessibility Features on Detail Page

Accessibility Features on Detail Page

Accessibility Features on Detail Page

The accessibility feature displayed on the detail page is based on your response to the accessibility features question during title setup. Features displayed to customers on the detail page are: Visual Adjustments, Nonvisual Reading, and Hazards. - Visual adjustments - Nonvisual reading - Hazards

Visual adjustments

This indicates whether your eBook allows readers to modify the appearance of the text and the page layout. Readers can make modifications, which can increase readability and make it easier to comprehend the text. Kindle books come in two different formats: - Reflowable Kindle books. This allows for the modification of the appearance by adapting to Kindle device’s screen size and reader’s chosen font and layout settings. Learn how to Prepare Reflowable and Print Books with Kindle Create for an optimal Kindle experience. - Fixed layout books such as print replica, manga, comics, and some children’s books or textbooks. With this format, books preserve their layout and structure and don’t allow for visual adjustments.

There are three possible descriptions readers will see for this attribute: - Not known if appearance can be modified: No information is available about the capability to adjust the text of this Kindle book. It’s unknown if you can modify the size, font, color, margins, spacing, and alignment. - Appearance cannot be modified: You can’t adjust the text of this Kindle book. You can’t modify the size, font, color, margins, spacing, and alignment. - Appearance can be modified: You can adjust the text of this Kindle book. You can modify the size, font, color, margins, spacing, and alignment.

Nonvisual reading

This indicates whether all content required for comprehension can be consumed in text and is accessible to users of assistive technologies. Some examples of compatible assistive technologies include screen readers and refreshable braille displays, typically used by people who are blind or have low vision. The text of most reflowable Kindle books is accessible. However, when your eBook includes non-text content such as images, photographs, graphs, tables, or videos, textual alternatives may be required for comprehension. Without the textual alternatives, the book won’t be considered readable for assistive technologies in read aloud and braille. Textual alternatives could include alt text, extended descriptions, transcripts, and captions. Currently, print replica and image-based fixed layout Kindle books aren’t readable in read aloud and braille. Note: Print replica and image-based fixed layout Kindle books are not readable in read aloud and braille. Compare Formats to help you determine how to prepare a book for an optimal Kindle experience. Kindle books do not currently support closed captions in audio/video content. There are four possible descriptions readers will see for this attribute: - Not known if readable in read aloud and braille: No information is available about the nonvisual reading aspects of this Kindle book. - Not readable in read aloud and braille: The text of this Kindle book isn’t accessible to screen readers. - Partially readable in read aloud and braille: The text of this Kindle book is accessible to screen readers, but some meaningful non-text content may not have text alternatives. - Readable in read aloud and braille: The text of this Kindle book is accessible to screen readers, and all meaningful non-text content has text alternatives.

Hazards

This indicates whether there are any potential hazards present in the Kindle book that could afflict physiologically sensitive readers. Potential hazards only exist within a Kindle book that contains audio and/or video content. There are four possible descriptions readers will see for this attribute: - No information available about potential hazards in this Kindle book. - This Kindle book contains the following hazards:

Video with flashing hazard. This refers to video content with flashing that occurs more than 3 times per second. - Video with motion simulation - Audio

Note: Audio and/or video files do not start automatically and must be initiated by the reader.

Accessibility for eBooks

Accessibility for eBooks

Accessibility for eBooks

As we continuously work to improve inclusive experiences for our customers, you will be able to provide information on accessibility features in your eBook. When you share accessibility features in your eBook content during title setup, you help contribute to an inclusive, accessible reading experience. Readers will know whether your eBook supports accessibility that will meet their individual needs to make informed purchasing decisions. - Provide accessibility information - Update accessibility information - View accessibility information - Accessibility best practices

Provide accessibility information

When publishing a new eBook or making changes that require republishing through KDP, you will be able to provide information about your eBook’s accessibility features during title setup, as part of the standard publishing process. Choose the response that best reflects your eBook’s accessibility features. The default selection is “I don’t know…” and you can proceed with publishing even with this selection. ##### How to update accessibility information To update your eBook’s accessibility information, follow the steps below. Bulk updating is not available. 1. Go to your Bookshelf 2. Select the ellipsis button (“…”) next to the book you want to update 3. Choose Edit eBook content 4. Complete necessary edits 5. Review other sections on page where other changes may be needed 6. Scroll to the Accessibility Features question 7. Choose the appropriate response to the question(s) 8. Select “Save and Continue”. This takes you to the Pricing page 9. Select “Publish” at the bottom of the Pricing page

How to view accessibility information

After your book is published and available on the detail page, you can see how your response to accessibility features in your eBook is displayed on the detail page. It can take up to 72 hours for accessibility information to show up. Visit Timelines to learn more about standard publication timelines. To view the accessibility features on the detail page: 1. Go to your eBook’s detail page 2. Look for the Accessibility icon in the book details section along with the other icons. 3. Click the “Learn more” link under the accessibility icon to view the book’s accessibility details

Note: While accessibility features are displayed on the detail page, updating your book details is separate. Book details do not influence how accessible your eBook content is. Visit Book Detail Resources and Update Your Book for additional information on book details. Read on for recommended best practices, and learn more on what accessibility features are displayed on your detail page. #### Accessibility best practices To create an inclusive reading experience for all readers, we recommend the following best practices to ensure your book is accessible to all readers, including those who are blind, have moderate-to-severe vision impairments, or have reading disabilities such as dyslexia. As we prioritize accessibility across our products and features, we regularly update these best practices based on industry standards to support the evolving accessibility needs of our customers. - Images - Multimedia audio/video content - Videos without Audio - Videos with Audio - Audio

  • Headings
  • Lists
  • Tables
Images

Images are visual information offered to sighted users. To benefit customers who cannot see the images in your content, including alternative text (“alt text”) for meaningful images in your content means screen readers can describe them to a blind reader. A meaningful image is something that conveys meaning to the reader. Consider whether the content of your book would make sense if the reader couldn’t see the image you include. An alternative text is a short description of the media that is focused on the page. If visual elements don’t have a text alternative, then customers with low or no vision will not have access to this information. While images can have text alternatives that assistive technology users can consume, where possible, we recommend authors use real text rather than an image of text. To support image accessibility, you can: - Provide alternative text. All images that provide information or context or further enhance the reader’s understanding of the content must have a text alternative. Keep alt text to a maximum of 140 characters. - Describe it in the surrounding text. Describe the image directly in the text. - Remove descriptions on decorative images. Set the alt attribute of decorative images to ‘null’ and avoid using images of text. - Use real text rather than an image of text. Do not rely solely on images to convey text-based information.

Multimedia audio/video content

Uploading audio-visual file content for your eBook’s manuscript is not common. KDP doesn’t accept Kindle Edition with audio/video content or support closed captions. The guidance below is informational only. ###### Videos without Audio When videos are pre-recorded without a main audio track (example: video-only media), a text transcript or audio track that describes the visual information in the video is required. Transcripts and audio descriptions give customers access to the information contained within a video without needing to see it. Providing transcripts and audio descriptions benefit people with limited or no vision, as well as anybody in a situation where they can’t fully see the video. ###### Videos with Audio When a video has an audio track, captions are required to convey the meaning of the audio. Captioning provides customers access to audio information when watching a video, benefiting people with limited or no hearing, as well as anybody in a situation where they can’t play or can’t fully understand the audio. Recommended ways to optimize videos with audio: - Keep captions synchronized with the audio, while also making sure they stay on-screen long enough for customers to read them. - Include all spoken words and meaningful sounds from the audio. - Follow a captioning style guide for consistency.

Audio

Narration (audio description) is required for pre-recorded video content without audio. Audio narration explains any important visuals that can’t be understood from the video, benefiting customers who can hear and understand speech, but do not clearly see the video if they are blind or have low vision. Provided audio description supports: - Customers who are blind. Hearing the audio description provides a richer, more coherent experience than a transcript. - Customers who have low vision. information from the audio description enhances their understanding of the video. - Customers watching a video on a small screen. They can gain similar benefits from audio description.

For an in-depth technical overview on developing a manuscript, visit our Guidelines for Specific Types of eBooks. ##### Language Making sure that your book’s content is in the language it is intended to be in benefits readers using assistive technology such as a screen readers, braille displays, or voice dictation. Helping users recognize language changes on screen can also ensure all readers can effectively engage with your content, regardless of how they access it. It is important that the language you select in the Bookshelf, the language in which the book is written, and the language specified in your content file’s metadata match. KDP currently supports over 45 languages. If your book includes multiple languages, select the primary language. ##### Content Structure Creating a meaningful order of content in sequence reflects the meaning of the content. Having structure to your content supports users of assistive technologies, such as screen reader users, or readers with cognitive disabilities so that they can better understand the layout of your book. For fixed-format books, consider the reading order of your headings to more efficiently navigate contents of your book. You can create well-structured content by adopting the following best practices. ###### Headings Headings help customers to navigate content more efficiently. When headings clearly reflect the topic or purpose, it makes content easier to locate, understand, and interact with. Use a logical, well-structured heading hierarchy to organize your book chapters, sections, and subsections. This will allow readers to quickly scan and grasp the structure of your book. Learn more on creating a table of contents. To create well-structured headings, you can: - Choose words that accurately describe the content within the section. - Keep headings brief while ensuring they provide enough information about the section’s content. - Put the most important information at the beginning of each heading. - Make sure headings indicate what customers can expect to find in the section, aiding their understanding and navigation. - Create headings that allow customers to anticipate the content, making it easier to process the information.

Lists

Use numbered and bulleted lists to group items and provide structure. By using the correct list format, assistive technology users can better navigate and orient themselves within a page of content, and screen reader users can navigate to (or over) lists accordingly. - Use bullet lists when the order of information isn’t important to the understanding of the content. - Use numbered lists when the specific order of information is important to understand or complete a series of steps.

Tables

Table cells are announced in reading order for the language. Like a sighted customer, screen readers will associate cells with the column and row headers to help users make sense of the information. In addition to contextual announcements, most screen readers support special navigation within tables. To ensure accessibility in your tables, you can: - Format your tables with column and/or row headings. Table headers let all users know how information in a table is related. - Create a caption for the table on a page. A caption is a name that describes the table and is displayed adjacent to the table. For example, place the word “Country codes” above a table showing information of different country codes. - Avoid using an image of a table. Information for large amounts of table content can be challenging to convey. An image of a table is not recommended.

Color

Considering the contrast between foreground and background can help ensure your content is accessible to people with vision-related disabilities such as colorblindness. Not relying on color alone to convey meaning can also help customers with low vision who may have trouble reading or finding important information on the page. To support color accessibility, you can: - Ensure text has sufficient contrast with background colors. If you have a dark background, the text or foreground should be light, and vice versa. The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines’ standards recommend a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1. - Check the font size and font style. Using very thin or small fonts can be difficult to read even with enough contrast between text and background. If using large fonts (18pt or larger or 14pt and bold), the contrast ratio is at least 3:1 against all backgrounds. If using regular-sized text, the foreground and background color has a contrast of at least 4.5:1. Tip: use a color contrast tool to check if your content has enough contrast. - Identify links in the body. Beyond the standard “blue” color, links can be identified with underlines, a border, or a change in font size and font style.

Authors & Contributors

Authors & Contributors

Your book should have at least one author or primary contributor. In addition to listing the author, you can list contributors. Contributors are people involved in creating your book, such as editors, illustrators, or anyone else you want to give credit to.

When entering the author name, be mindful of spelling and accuracy as this field cannot be changed once your book is published. This applies to paperbacks, hardcover, and eBooks. Author name is one of the most common ways customers will search for your books, so it’s important to ensure it’s consistent with other books associated with the author. Additionally, several Amazon features (e.g., Author Pages, Series Pages, format linking) rely on a consistent author name. If the primary contributor’s name is similar to a popular author’s name, consider using a pen name, middle name, or adding an initial. ##### Paperback, Hardcover and eBook Differences - The middle name/initial right after the first name - The prefix before the author’s first name - The suffix right after the author’s last name

Note that hardcover is currently unsupported in JP. ##### Can I use pen names to publish my book? ##### Can my book have multiple authors? ##### What are Author Pages? ##### Can I update my book’s author or contributor’s field?
