Books Titles & Editions

Books Titles & Editions

Title best practices
  • Enter your title exactly as it reads on the cover of your book. The title field will show your book’s title on the book’s detail page in the Amazon website.
  • Ensure your title is exactly the same for your paperback, hardcover, and eBook versions. This is how they are linked together on a single detail page.
  • Don’t add anything from the following list of prohibited items in the title field:
  • Repeating generic keywords like “notebook,” “journal,” “gifts,” “books,” etc.
  • Unauthorized reference to other titles or authors
  • Unauthorized reference to a trademarked term
  • Reference to sales rank (e.g., “bestselling”)
  • Reference to advertisements or promotions (e.g., “free”)
  • Only Punctuation (e.g. “!!!!!!!!”)
  • Using only “unknown”, “n/a”, “na”, “blank”, “none”, “null”, “not applicable”
  • HTML tags
Subtitles

A subtitle is an optional secondary title that contains additional information about the content of your book. Together, your title and subtitle must be 200 characters or less. Your subtitle should adhere to the same guidelines as your title above. For example, Mary Shelley gave her most famous novel the title “Frankenstein”; with a subtitle of “The Modern Prometheus”. Her book can be called and is recognizable by both names. By using the subtitle “The Modern Prometheus”, she references the Greek Titan as a hint of the novel’s themes. ##### Editions An edition is a particular version of your book. The edition number tells readers whether the book is an original version or an updated version. Books that change frequently or go through annual updates (such as textbooks) need to have edition numbers. If this is the first time you have published this book and you anticipate future editions, enter the numeral 1. If the book was previously published and the version you are publishing contains significant changes, enter the numeral 2 (and so on). Each time you make significant changes to your book, it is considered a new edition. Significant changes include updates to the core book details (author name, cover, title, etc.) and manuscript updates that result in page count changes by more than 10%. Updates to certain book details, sometimes called metadata, also require a new edition. These book details include, title, primary author name, ISBN, trim size, and ink and paper type. To create a new edition of your book, repeat the process to create a new title and include the appropriate number in the Edition number field so that readers know that the book is an updated version of a previously published book. Small changes such as typos or capitalization fixes do not require a new edition number. ##### Can I update my book’s title and/or edition? You won’t be able to update your book’s title and/or edition once your book has been published, but you can publish it with the updates as a new title. See our help page to create a book. When submitting it as a new book, you’re required to include the following disclaimer at the top of the description field: - Significant changes to both book title and author name aren’t allowed. - Changes such as typos or capitalization errors in your title do not require a new edition. Contact us and we will help you correct it.

Change or view your ISBN

Change or view your ISBN

You can update your ISBN if your book is still in draft. This article explains how to view your ISBN on KDP and what to do if you need to make changes. ##### View your ISBN There are two ways to view your ISBN information: 1. If your book is published and available on Amazon, you can view the ISBN details on your book’s product page. Note: You can access your book’s product page from the KDP Bookshelf by clicking View on Amazon under the book you want to see. 2. To view your book’s ISBN details from KDP, go the Content tab in your book’s setup. Scroll to the ISBN section.

Change your ISBN

ISBNs cannot be changed if your book is published. If you need to update the book’s ISBN or other details, such as title or author name, you’ll have to unpublish the book and then publish a new edition (creating a book the same way you did the first time). The new edition should use the updated details. For instructions on unpublishing and republishing, read this article. To change the ISBN for a book that’s never been published: 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf. 2. Click the ellipsis button (“…”) next to the book you want to update. 3. Select Edit [Book] Content. 4. In the ISBN section, update the relevant details. Tip: If you want to remove your own ISBN and use on another book, update the ISBN option to the Get a free KDP ISBN option. 5. Hit Save and continue.

Note: If you’re using your own ISBN and updated the book details there, it’ll take 5 business days for KDP to register those changes. After those 5 business days, you can update your book on KDP. This will avoid any errors between our system and the ISBN agency’s.

Color Ink Options

Printing differences between standard and premium color ink
  • Standard color is ideal for books with a high page count, and interiors with fewer images, where a balance between cost and quality is needed. Paperbacks printed in standard color have a matte finish and are different in sharpness and richness of color as those printed in premium color.
  • Premium color is ideal for image-heavy color interiors, like children’s books, cookbooks, or photography books, where image sharpness and clarity are pivotal.
Differences in detail page listings

  • If your book is already published, the interior and paper type is locked. After publication, you can’t change your ink type between Standard color, Premium color, and black-and-white.

Convert a Paperback Word File to PDF

Convert a Paperback Word File to PDF

  • Draft view. Go to the View tab and click on Draft in the “Views” section
  • Show formatting button. Go to the Home tab and click the Show/Hide Formatting (¶) button in the “Paragraph” section
  • Reveal formatting pane. Hold the “Shift” key and type “F1.” Click on any content to view how the text is formatted and see links to the menus to make adjustments. You can also use the compare option to see how formatting differs from one selection to another
  • Navigation pane. Go to the View tab and click Navigation Pane in the “Show” section. When the pane opens, click Pages. This can help you see if page sizes differ
  1. Go to File > Print
  2. Select the AdobePDF printer and click on Printer Properties
  3. On the Adobe PDF settings tab, click the Add button next to Adobe PDF Page Size
  4. Give the page size a name, add dimensions, then click the Add/Modify button

  • Check your sections. To have separate page numbering for a section, unlink it from the previous section. To unlink sections, go to the Header/Footer toolbar

  • Set default printer to Adobe PDF before converting. Word re-paginates depending on the default printer

  • Search for unwanted page breaks. With the Show Formatting view selected, you’ll be able to see page breaks and remove them.

  • Check Paragraph/Indents and Spacing settings. Make sure Spacing Before and/or Spacing After values aren’t set too high

  • Check Paragraph/Line and Page Breaks and review settings for:Page Break Before. This inserts page breaks before paragraphs

  • Keep With Next. This prevents page breaks between current and following paragraphs

  • Keep Lines Together. This prevents page breaks within a paragraph

  • Use “Next page” section breaks. If you still have problems, change Section Break > Next page to Section Break > Continuous

  • If using mirror margins, use an even page section break

  • Hard page breaks (Ctrl + Enter) can be troublesome in Word. They can cause blank pages if used after a page break

  • Select the last paragraph. On the Home tab, go to Paragraphs > Line and Page Breaks > Pagination. Make sure all the boxes are unchecked.

  • On the View Tab, check show Navigation Pane. Select the page and go to the Page Layout tab. Then highlight that page and go to Page Setup > Layout > Page > Vertical alignment and make sure that it says Top and not Center. To apply this setting to the whole file, select all and ensure the setting is for Top.

  • Word downsamples images by default when saving. Change this by going to File > Word Options > Advanced and check the “Do not compress images in file” box

  • Size your image to the intended size before placing in your Word file. Sizing up or down after placement will reduce resolution

  • Place your images; do not drag and drop. Drag and drop will reduce resolution

  • Choosing “Print to PDF” instead of “Save As PDF” will allow your images to remain at 300 PPI (pixels per inch)

  • Images missing? Go to File > Options > Display > Printing Options and check either or both, the “Print Background Colors and Images” box and the “Print Drawings Created in Word” box

  • Images still missing? This is often due to using a third-party PDF producer. Try a different producer

  1. Set Adobe PDF printer as the default printer. Under the File > Options > Advanced > Layout options dialog setting, check “Use printer metrics to lay out document”
  2. Go to File > Print, select the AdobePDF printer, and click on Printer Properties
  3. On the Adobe PDF settings tab, select “PDF/X-1a.” If this option is not available on your system, select “High-Quality Print” or “Press Quality” from the list of presets

  • Word uses the default printer to display your document. Always use Adobe PDF or PDFMaker as the default printer to ensure that the Word file appears the same when using a different computer

  • Fonts that are installed on one computer may not be on another. In this case, the font will be replaced. The size and spacing of characters can vary significantly from one font to another. This can dramatically change the formatting

  • Rename the file. This can overwrite erroneous data introduced in previous saves.

  • Copy to a new document. Filed data is stored at the end of the document. Turn on Show formatting to see formatting marks. Copy everything but the last paragraph tag (¶), then paste into a new document.

  • Save the file as XML. This will fix file structure issues. The XML file can then be re-saved as a Word document.

  • Save the file as TXT. This will remove all formatting and any formatting errors that have been introduced to the file. Copy everything and paste into a new document. Then you can re-format your file.

  • CTRL+Space. This removes all character-level formatting. Select text, then hold CTRL and press the space bar to remove fonts, underlining, boldface, and italics to return text to the default.

  • CTRL+Q. This removes all paragraph-level formatting. Select text, then hold QTRL and press Q to remove any line spacing, line before/after paragraphs, indents, etc.

  • Convert the file to Rich Text Format (RTF) to preserve formatting. Re-open the RTF file in Word for Mac and convert it back to its native format. This can remove file damage

  • Copy everything except the last paragraph mark (¶) to a new document. The paragraph mark “holds” certain style and section formatting in Word for Mac. Leaving this mark behind will sometimes remove file damage

  • Click Select All from Edit menu, hold down Shift and press the Left Arrow key once. Release the Shift key

  • Click Copy from the Edit menu and then click New Blank Document from the File menu

  • In the new document, click Paste from Edit menu. You can then reapply style and section formatting

  • Copy all to a text-only file and then copy back to a new blank document in Word for Mac. This will remove all formatting and hopefully file damage from the file. But this will also require re-formatting

Delay or cancel a pre-order release

Delay or cancel a pre-order release

This article shares more information about delaying or cancelling your pre-order. ##### Delay release date You can delay your release date up to 30 days, without penalty, as a one-time exclusion. This one time exclusion applies to your whole catalog, not just the postponed book. You won’t be able to set up a new pre-order for one year or extend release dates for other existing pre-orders if you delay a pre-order more than once. ###### How to delay a pre-order release: 1. Go to your Bookshelf. 2. Select the ellipsis button (“…”) under KINDLE EBOOK ACTIONS next to the eBook you want to update. 3. Choose Edit eBook details. 4. In the Pre-order section, click Edit release date. 5. Enter the new date and click OK. 6. Go to Kindle eBook Rights & Pricing. 7. Select Save and continue. 8. Scroll to bottom of page and Submit for pre-order.

Customers who pre-ordered the eBook will receive an email telling them you delayed the release. ##### Cancel a release A pre-order release will be cancelled if you unpublish the eBook, miss the submission deadline, or by request. Cancellation of a pre-order’s release date is applicable for pre-order eBooks in the ‘Pre-order Live’ status. If you cancel a scheduled pre-order, you won’t be able to set up any other eBook for pre-order for one year. ###### How to cancel a pre-order: 1. Go to your Bookshelf. 2. Select the ellipsis button (“…”) under KINDLE EBOOK ACTIONS next to the eBook you want to update. 3. Select Unpublish eBook. 4. You’ll see a message displayed to inform you that if you unpublish and cancel the pre-order, you won’t be able to set up any other eBook for pre-order for one year. 5. If you would like to continue, click Unpublish.

After you unpublish the eBook, your pre-order will be cancelled and no further edits can be made to the title. ###### Related articles - Pre-order statuses - Kindle eBook pre-order

Fixing errors or formatting with book descriptions

Fixing errors or formatting with book descriptions

If your book description isn’t displaying correctly, here’s how you can solve any issues, whether it’s HTML related or the formatting is off. ##### Troubleshooting book description errors If you get an error, such as “Description may not contain invisible characters” or “Please fix the highlighted issue,” this means there are hidden or unsupported characters in the HTML source code. This can happen when copying and pasting content directly from a document into KDP. Sometimes it’ll copy over unsupported HTML characters. To fix this, we recommend manually typing in your book description. Alternatively, you can review the source code of your book description and ensure you only use supported HTML from our Help article. To review the source code of your book description: 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf. 2. Click the ellipsis button (“…”) next to the book you want to edit. 3. Select Edit [book] details. 4. Scroll down to the Description section. 5. Click Source. 6. Review the HTML against our supported characters.

Solving formatting issues

If your book description isn’t appearing as you intended on Amazon, it’s most likely due to HTML used in the source code. Even if you didn’t manually add any, this can happen if you copy & pasted directly from another document into KDP. For example, if you notice all your content is bolded when it shouldn’t be, check the source code. Are there Header tags being used, where they shouldn’t be? Is there an opening tag and a closing tag to all formatted text? For a full list of supported HTML, please review this list.

Fixing typos on a book title or author name

Fixing typos on a book title or author name

Some book details are locked after publishing. In certain scenarios, we can make updates, while in others, we cannot. ##### Fixing small typos If you’ve noticed a typo in your book title or author name, and your book has been published, you can ask KDP Support to make the correction. Note: This only applies to typos, e.g. misspelling of a name. We cannot make the updates while the book is “In Review.” If you used your own ISBN (i.e. not the free KDP ISBN), you’ll also need to make sure the details match with the ISBN agency. Otherwise, there’ll be publishing errors. ##### Changes other than typos If you need to update your book title or author name, other than a typo, you will need to republish your book as a new edition. Examples include shortening a book title or changing the author name to a pen name. ##### To unpublish and republish a corrected book You’ll follow the same steps to creating a new book as before, but instead you’ll use updated details. 1. Go to your Bookshelf. 2. Click the ellipsis button (“…”) next to the book you want to unpublish. 3. Click Unpublish.

Note: It takes up to 72 hours for a book to unpublish. Individual book formats (i.e. paperback vs eBook) can be unpublished and republished.

Get an ISBN

Get an ISBN

You can use a free ISBN provided by KDP or purchase your own from an official ISBN agency. This article explains both options and walks you through how to get and use an ISBN on KDP. ##### Get free ISBN from KDP Free ISBNs are only available for paperback and hardcover books. Choosing this option means KDP will register an ISBN, using your book details, with Bowker (US ISBN agency). To get a free KDP ISBN: 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf. 2. Click the ellipsis button (“…”) next to the book you want to add an ISBN to. 3. Select Edit Paperback Content or Edit Hardcover content. 4. In the ISBN section, choose Get free KDP ISBN. 5. Click Assign ISBN.

Note: Low-content books are not eligible for free ISBNs. ##### Purchase your own ISBN You can buy an ISBN from agencies like Bowker and use them to publish a book on KDP. This ISBN can be used to publish the same book on other publishing services. Make sure it’s registered with the correct title, author name, format, and imprint (i.e. publisher name). Bowker does offer discounted rates for KDP authors, if you’d like to buy an ISBN from them. To use a purchased ISBN on KDP: 1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf. 2. Click the ellipsis button (“…”) next to the book you want to add an ISBN to. 3. Select Edit Paperback Content or Edit Hardcover content. 4. In the ISBN section, choose Add your own ISBN. 5. Enter the details. We recommend copying and pasting directly from the ISBN agency to avoid mismatch errors.

Note: You don’t need an ISBN for eBooks on KDP. ##### Summary of ISBN Options - ISBN options: Cost: Publishing: Publisher Imprint: Publisher field in the Book’s detail page: Requirements - KDP Free ISBN: Free: Only with KDP: Automatically registered as “Independently published” in Bowker: It will show imprint name “Independently published”.: We’ll register your free ISBN, so no further requirements are needed from your end. - Your own ISBN: You cover the cost of the ISBN: You can publish outside of KDP: Register your own imprint with Bowker or local ISBN agency: It will show the imprint name you enter to publish your book.: When entering your book’s details ensure the information you are providing matches with the information you’ve registered in Bowker. You won’t be able to publish your book if there are any mismatches between this information. The Imprint field has a limit of 100 characters.

Groundwood Paper

Groundwood Paper

Introduction

Groundwood paper is available as an alternative to white and cream paper for all eligible paperbacks. To learn more about groundwood paper and its benefits, please review the FAQs below. ##### Contents - Eligibility and updating your paperbacks - Technical specifications

Why is groundwood paper a good choice for readers?

Groundwood paper is a lower carbon option perfect for paperback novels and text-heavy books. Because of its higher opacity and textured feel, it makes pages easier to read and turn. Additionally, print-on-demand books made from groundwood paper have at least 15% fewer CO2-equivalent emissions compared to other paper types. For the remaining residual carbon emissions of entire Groundwood paper book, we are applying high-quality carbon credits from Amazon’s carbon credit service. For complete eligibility requirements and technical specifications, visit our Paperback Submission Guidelines Help page. ###### Which books are eligible? Groundwood paper is eligible for paperbacks with black and white interiors in all trim sizes. Books that meet these criteria will be marked with a green banner and a leaf icon on your Bookshelf. The leaf icon serves as a clear, universal symbol of nature and environmental consciousness, making it easy to identify titles that can be updated to be more eco-friendly and help you make environmentally conscious manufacturing decisions. ###### Which books are not eligible? Books that have heavy ink coverage are not eligible or recommended for groundwood paper to prevent the ink from showing through the pages. If we encounter issues when printing these books, KDP reserves the right to change the paper to cream or white to ensure quality. ###### In which marketplaces is groundwood paper available? Groundwood paper is available in all marketplaces where KDP paperbacks are supported: - Amazon.com - Amazon.ca - Amazon.co.uk - Amazon.de - Amazon.es - Amazon.fr - Amazon.it - Amazon.nl - Amazon.ie - Amazon.com.be - Amazon.pl - Amazon.se - Amazon.com.au - Amazon.co.jp

Can I use groundwood paper for books enrolled in Expanded Distribution (EDC)?

Yes, but eligibility depends on your trim size. Before changing your paper type, check the trim size eligibility chart on the Expanded Distribution Help page to confirm your book is still eligible. ###### How can I switch my existing books to groundwood? You can convert your existing books to groundwood paper in two ways, one by one, or using the bulk conversion feature. To convert your titles one by one: Simply update your book’s Ink & Paper type and submit the update by following these instructions: 1. Sign into your KDP account. 2. Go to your Bookshelf. 3. Under the book you want to update, click the ellipsis button (“…”). 4. Select Edit Paperback Content. 5. Under Print Options, update the ink and paper type to groundwood. 6. Click Save and continue. 7. Publish your Paperback Book to complete your submission.

For bulk conversion: Use the bulk update tool to convert multiple eligible titles at once. Only titles that don’t require cover updates will appear in the bulk update tool. Important: If your book exceeds 350 pages (cream paper) or 525 pages (white paper), the spine section of your cover dimensions will require adjustments. This is due to the thickness of groundwood paper. Check our cover calculator to determine if your book requires updates. If you need to adjust your book, visit our help page for instructions to Update Your Cover. ###### How can I confirm that my titles have been switched to groundwood? When you switch a title to groundwood and submit your changes, your title’s status will update from “Live” to “In Review,” then “Publishing,” and back to “Live” once the conversion is complete. For quick conversions, you may not see any status change. Your title will remain “Live” throughout the process. To confirm your title is using groundwood paper: - Check Title Setup to verify the paper type is set to groundwood - Your title will no longer show the groundwood eligibility indicator on your Bookshelf - Your title will no longer appear in the bulk update tool (because it’s already using groundwood)

Are there any changes in the printing costs when using groundwood paper?

Groundwood printing costs per page are approximately 5% lower than cream and white paper with black and white ink. This pricing applies to all titles using groundwood paper — including existing live titles. No action is needed on your part. Want to see how this impacts your printing costs and royalties? Use our Printing Cost & Royalty Calculator to compare printing costs and royalties per paper type. For complete pricing details by marketplace, visit our Paperback Printing Costs Help page. ###### Can I order proof copies with groundwood paper? Yes, to order a proof copy from your Bookshelf, first change the paper type of the book. Then follow the instructions on this Help article to order the proof copy. Note: If you recently updated your book, and ordered a new copy, you may receive a copy from inventory that was printed prior to the changes. While we operate on a print-on-demand model, when a copy is printed on demand and the order is later canceled, that copy remains in inventory until sold. Books printed from a previous file are not eligible for replacement or refund. ##### Technical Specifications For complete technical specifications, including maximum page counts, spine calculations, and cover requirements, visit our Paperback Submission Guidelines Help page.

Kindle eBook Pre-Order

Kindle eBook Pre-Order

You can set up eBook pre-orders to start promoting your book before it’s released, through channels such as Author Central, Goodreads, your personal website, and elsewhere. Pre-orders will contribute toward sales rank and other Kindle Store merchandising even before your eBook’s released, helping more readers discover your eBook. This article explains what a pre-order is, and important reminders before selecting your eBook for pre-order. Note: Pre-order is currently available for eBooks. For paperbacks, you can schedule a Release Date. ##### What is pre-order? Pre-order allow customers to order your eBook as early as one year before the eBook is released and available for download. You can set up eBooks for pre-order in Kindle Stores worldwide when creating an eBook. When you submit an eBook for pre-order, your eBook content will not be available for download yet. However, an Amazon detail page will be published for customers to be able to pre-order the eBook. Note: If you upload a manuscript at the time of submitting your pre-order, Amazon may allows readers to preview samples of your book. Books without an ISBN, such as low-content books will not display a reading sample. Learn more about Read Sample. When your eBook is published on the scheduled release date, your eBook content will be delivered to customers who have ordered it. ##### Pre-order reminders - Eligibility: You can only set up a pre-order for new eBook titles. You can create up to 10 pre-order titles at a time. After each book release, you can set up additional pre-orders. Public domain eBooks aren’t eligible for pre-order. - Deadline for pre-order submission: To successfully set up a pre-order, you must upload your final manuscript and submit the pre-order more than 72 hours in advance of the scheduled release date. Failure to submit the pre-order on time will result in a pre-order cancellation. This will prevent you from setting up a pre-order on any eBook for one year. - Making updates to pre-order: You will not be able to update your pre-order after submitting your final manuscript for up to 72 hours. This is to ensure your eBook meet our publishing guidelines. After the review process is completed, you may make changes to your manuscript or eBook details. Review pre-order statuses for more information. - Cancelling a pre-order release: if you choose to cancel a pre-order release, such as unpublishing your eBook, you will not be able to set up any pre-orders for one year. Review delay or cancel a release for more information. - KDP Select. You can enroll your pre-order eBook in KDP Select, and the KDP Select term will begin on the eBook’s release date. You can only schedule Free Book Promotions, and Kindle Countdown Deals after the book’s release.

Low-Content Books

Low-Content Books

A low-content book has minimal or no content on the interior pages. Low-content books are generally repetitive, and designed to be filled in by the user. This does not typically include activity books, such as puzzle books or coloring books, which generally do not feature repetitive content on each page. See common examples of low-content books in the table below, but note that there can be exceptions. Low-content books do not require an ISBN. If you want an ISBN for your low-content book, you can use your own ISBN, or publish without an ISBN. Low-content books are not eligible for the free KDP ISBN. See the differences between using your own ISBN and publishing without an ISBN below. ##### Contents ##### Examples of low-content books - Low-Content: Not Generally Low-Content - Notebooks: Novels - Planners: Nonfiction - Diaries/Journals: Puzzle books - Prompt journals: Coloring books - Log books (i.e., tracking habits, activity, thankfulness): Photography - Coupon books: Sheet music - Score card templates: Manuals - Crafting templates (i.e., scrapbook paper, ephemera books, etc.): Textbooks - Blank sheet music (also known as manuscript or staff paper): Children’s books

How to create a low-content book
  1. Go to your Bookshelf.
  2. Click + Create new title or series and then select Create paperback or Create hardcover.
  3. Enter your information for each section as follows:

Paperback or Hardcover details. Enter your title, description, keywords, etc. Under Categories you need to check the Low-content box. Please note that if you do not select this box, or select a different box, your book will be rejected. 4. Paperback or Hardcover content. Under Print ISBN, you can choose between Publish without an ISBN or Use my own ISBN. Upload your manuscript and cover files, preview your book, and order a proof. 5. Paperback or Hardcover rights and pricing. Choose the territories where you hold distribution rights and set your list price. 6. After entering your information, click Publish Your Paperback Book or Publish Your Hardcover Book.

What type of barcode will appear on a low-content book?
What information can be updated after publishing a low-content book?
Changing your ISBN option
Differences between using your own ISBN and publishing without an ISBN
  • Expanded Distribution: Expanded Distribution is not supported for low-content books, regardless of the ISBN option you select. Learn more about enrollment requirements.
  • Read Sample (Look Inside the Book) feature: The sample and the back cover thumbnail are currently not supported for low-content books published without ISBN. If you’d like to activate this feature for your book, we recommend you to buy your own ISBN from Bowker or through your local ISBN agency. Learn more about using your own ISBN.

Alternatively, you can use A+ Content to add images of your book’s interior so buyers can see what it looks like. These images will appear on your book detail page. Learn more about A+ Content. - Series: Low-content books are not eligible for creating a series, regardless of the ISBN option you select. Learn more about series. - Transparency codes: Low-content books that are published without an ISBN are not eligible for Transparency codes. Note: Transparency codes are being retired from KDP print barcodes and are not available for books created after November 2025. Learn more about barcodes.

Make Your Book More Discoverable with Keywords

Make Your Book More Discoverable with Keywords

Make Your Book More Discoverable with Keywords

Contents
  • How to add and update keywords
  • Best practices
  • Useful keyword types
  • Keywords to avoid
  • Other metadata and keyword tips
How to add and update keywords
  1. Go to your Bookshelf and click the ellipsis button (“…”) next to your book.
  2. Select Edit book details for your book format.
  3. Under the Keywords section, add/edit your keywords.
  4. Go to the bottom of the page, and click Save and Continue.
  5. Once you reach the book Pricing page, click the Publish button at the bottom of the page.
Best practices
  • Combine keywords in the most logical order. Customers search for “military science fiction” but probably not for “fiction science military”
  • Use up to seven keywords or short phrases. Keep an eye on the character limit in the text field
  • Before publishing, search using keywords you’re considering on Amazon. If you get irrelevant or unsatisfying results, make some changes. When searching, look at the suggestions that appear in the “Search” field drop down
  • Think like a reader. Imagine how you’d search if you were a customer
Useful keyword types
  • Setting (Colonial America)
  • Character types (single dad, veteran)
  • Character roles (strong female lead)
  • Plot themes (coming of age, forgiveness)
  • Story tone (dystopian, feel-good)
Keywords to avoid
  • Information covered elsewhere in your book’s metadata (title, contributors, etc.)
  • Words already mentioned in your book categories (e.g. 19th Century History)
  • Subjective claims about quality (e.g. “best novel ever”)
  • Time-sensitive statements (“new,” “on sale,” “available now”)
  • Information common to most items in the category (“book”)
  • Spelling errors
  • Variants of spacing, punctuation, capitalization, and pluralization (“80GB” and “80 GB,” “computer” and “computers”, etc.). Exception: Words translated in more than one way (e.g. “Mao Zedong” or “Mao Tse-tung,” “Hanukkah” or “Chanukah”
  • Anything misrepresentative like the name of an author not associated with your book. This kind of information can create a confusing customer experience. Kindle Direct Publishing has a zero tolerance policy for metadata that is meant to advertise, promote, or mislead
  • Brands that you do not own or that you are unauthorized to use
  • Quotation marks in search terms. Single words work better than phrases, and specific words work better than general ones. If you enter “complex suspenseful whodunit,” only people who type all of those words will find your book. For better results, enter this: complex suspenseful whodunit. Customers can search for any of those words and find your book
  • Amazon program names like as “Kindle Unlimited” or “KDP Select”
  • HTML tags
Other metadata and keyword tips
  • Customers are more likely to skim past long titles (over 60 characters)
  • Focus your book’s description on the book’s content
  • Make sure your book’s metadata adhere to KDP’s guidelines
  • Your keywords can capture useful, relevant information that won’t fit in your title and description (setting, character, plot, theme, etc.)
  • You can change keywords and descriptions as often as you like
  • If your book is available in different formats (physical, audio), keep your keywords and description consistent across formats

Pre-order pricing and sales reports

Pre-order pricing and sales reports

In this article, you can learn more about setting your pre-order’s list price and pre-order sales reports. ##### List price Set the list price for your pre-order book based on our list price requirements. You can change your list price during the pre-order period, but if you lower it, we’ll retroactively charge that lower price to customers who already pre-ordered your book. If you raise the price during pre-order, all prior customers will pay the lower price. Your royalty will be based on the actual price we charge customers. This doesn’t apply to Amazon.de and/or Amazon.in. Note: Pre-order books listed on Amazon.de are subject to the German fixed price law. If you increase the price during the pre-order period, all prior orders are canceled. We’ll notify customers who bought your book about the new price and provide details for how they can buy the book again. ##### Pricing your book When you enter your list price, you get an estimated royalty that’s based on the royalty plan you choose. If you choose the 70% royalty plan without uploading the manuscript you’d like delivered to customers, the estimated royalty will reflect delivery cost for a file size of a typical eBook. Delivery cost can change based on the size of your final file. We recommend using the grid on the Kindle eBook Pricing setup page to understand how file size and delivery costs can affect royalties. ##### Pre-order report Your pre-order report is updated as orders are placed. This report includes pre-ordered units, pre-order cancellations, and net pre-order units. Your pre-order sales data will not appear in other reports until after your eBook is delivered to customers on its release date. After that, you’ll see pre-order units listed in the Prior Months’ Royalties report, under the “Pre-order” transaction type. Once your eBook is released and customers start downloading their copies, you’ll receive credit for final sales. Learn more about pre-order payment timelines. ##### Royalties Learn more about eBook royalty plan options.

Price Troubleshooting

Price Troubleshooting

Frequently Asked Questions

We reserve the right to set the retail customer price for books you publish with us, which may be different than your list price. Keep in mind that you set and control the list price of your work, while the price on the detail page and any discounts are set at the discretion of Amazon, and are subject to change.

Here are two examples of when this could happen: - The price at which a competitor sells your book is lower than your list price. - The price at which we sell a physical edition of your book is lower than your eBook’s list price.

For eBooks:

If you chose the 70% royalty option, your royalties are calculated from the retail customer price (if the sale qualifies for the 70% royalty option). If you chose the 35% option, your royalties are calculated from the list price you set.

For paperback and hardcover:

We retain discretion to set the retail customer price for books we sell. Our decision to price products is based on a number of considerations, which vary over time. We suggest you set your book’s list price based on what you deem is a fair value for customers. Royalties will continue to be calculated from the list price you provided in your KDP account. Print royalty rates can be either 50% or 60%, depending on list price and marketplace. Use the following chart to determine the royalty rate of your book: - Marketplace: 50% royalty rate for list prices at or below:: 60% royalty rate for list prices at or above: - Amazon.com: 9.98 USD: 9.99 USD - Amazon.de Amazon.fr Amazon.it Amazon.es Amazon.nl: 9.98 EUR: 9.99 EUR - Amazon.co.uk: 7.98 GBP: 7.99 GBP - Amazon.ca: 13.98 CAD: 13.99 CAD - Amazon.com.au: 13.98 AUD: 13.99 AUD - Amazon.co.jp: 999 JPY: 1000 JPY - Amazon.pl: 39 PLN: 40 PLN - Amazon.se: 98 SEK: 99 SEK

  • Terms and Conditions
  • Pricing Page
  • List Price Requirements

Updates to your book’s list price may vary: - For eBooks, it can take up to 24 hours. - For paperback and hardcover, it can take 3 to 5 days.

To update the list price of your book, follow the steps outlined on our pricing page. No, you can’t set your book’s list price as free.

An alternative for eBooks: You can enroll in KDP Select and use the Free eBook Promotion. This allows you to give away your eBook for free, up to 5 days (within each 90-day term). If your book is available through Amazon, third-party sellers have the ability to purchase your book and re-sell it through Amazon or other retail channels. Amazon is not directly affiliated with these sellers, and we do not control certain aspects of their Amazon product listing. This includes pricing, shipping, condition (new or used), and delivery terms. If you set multiple list prices for different Amazon marketplaces in the EU, we use the lowest of these list prices. For example, if you provide different list prices for a book on Amazon.de and Amazon.fr, when we sell your book to customers that are eligible to purchase from both websites, we use the lower of the two list prices. We do this to provide consistency across our Amazon marketplaces.

Customers from countries outside the US may shop on Amazon.com. For example, a UK customer might buy a book off of Amazon.com instead of Amazon.co.uk. When this happens, we will convert your list price to USD for that sale.

For print books, the price on the detail page might be different than the list price you set in your KDP account. You will still be paid royalties based on your list price. The 70% royalty will only apply to sales in the Available Sales Territories. Your sales to customers outside the Available Sales Territories will fall under the 35% Royalty Option. You can change your pre-order’s list price or book details any time before the submission deadline. To view your submission deadline, you can use the timer found on your eBook setup pages. The deadline is 3 days before the release date. - If you lower your list price, we’ll retroactively charge that amount to customers who have already pre-ordered your book. Additionally, you’ll receive royalties based on the lower price. - If you increase the list price during the pre-order period, all prior customers will still pay the lower price for all marketplaces where your book will be sold, except for Germany. We base your royalty on the retail customer price. For Germany, all prior orders placed will be cancelled. We will notify customers who bought your book with the new price and provide details for them to buy the book again.

You can calculate your printing cost and royalty using our calculator. KDP prints your book on demand and subtracts your printing costs from your royalties. That means you don’t have to pay any costs upfront or carry any inventory.

Printing cost also depends on which Amazon marketplace (website) a reader ordered your book from. Costs also vary depending on trim size, page count, and ink type (black ink or color ink). Trim sizes, bleed settings and cover finish don’t affect printing cost.

Note: Figures generated by the calculator are for estimation purposes only. Your actual royalty will be calculated when you set up your book.

How to update your book’s price

  1. Go to your KDP Bookshelf.

  2. Click the ellipsis button (“…”) next to the book you want to update.

  3. Choose Edit eBook Pricing.

  4. In the “Royalty and Pricing” section, make the changes.

  5. Click the Publish Your Kindle eBook button at the bottom of the page.

  6. Go to your KDP Bookshelf.

  7. Click the ellipsis button (“…”) next to the book you want to update.

  8. Choose Edit rights & pricing. For published books, choose Edit print book pricing.

  9. In the “Pricing & Royalty” section, make the changes.

  10. Click the Publish Your Paperback Book or Publish Your Hardcover Book button at the bottom of the page.

Cover finish
  • Glossy finish is shiny. It makes black covers darker and artwork more striking. It’s typical for textbooks, children’s books, and nonfiction.

Environmental consciousness

Environmental consciousness is important to us. As a manufacture-on-demand company, we produce units as they’re ordered, which reduces excess production. We also maintain a commitment to recycling waste materials resulting from the printing process and from daily office operations, and we will continue to review our practices to ensure we are doing our part to protect the environment. For information on EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), visit EU Deforestation Regulation Compliance.

Reschedule a pre-order release

Reschedule a pre-order release

Reschedule a release

Rescheduling an eBook pre-order’s release date is applicable for eBooks in a ‘Pre-order Live’ status. If you want to reschedule the release date for your submitted pre-order, you must re-submit and republish the eBook. Note: You cannot move a release date to be published on the same day because it takes up to 72 hours to prepare your eBook for delivery to customers. Tip:* If you want to release your eBook without waiting for the scheduled date, you’ve the option to select ‘I’m ready to release my book now’ in the “Pre-order” section. Note that this option is only available if you’re still within the pre-order submission deadline, your eBook is in ‘Pre-Order Draft’ status, and your manuscript is ready for publishing.* ##### To reschedule a release date: 1. Go to your Bookshelf. 2. Select the ellipsis button (“…”) under KINDLE EBOOK ACTIONS next to the eBook you want to update. 3. Choose Edit eBook details. 4. In the Pre-order section, click Edit release date. 5. Enter the new date and click OK. 6. Go to Kindle eBook Rights & Pricing. 7. Select Save and continue. 8. Scroll to bottom of page and Submit for pre-order.

Customers who pre-ordered the eBook will receive the content on the earlier release date. ###### Related articles - Pre-order statuses - Delay or cancel a release

How it works
  • The Amazon detail page (where your book can be purchased) will remain hidden until that date.
  • Your book will become available for purchase at 12:00 AM GMT on the release date.
  • Changes can be made to your book or release date before the publication deadline. This deadline will appear in a countdown timer on your book’s setup pages.
  • Five days prior to your book release, we will start preparing to deliver your book to customers worldwide. During this time, you will not be able to make updates to your manuscript file, update your book’s details, or unpublish your book. You will be able to make updates to your book again after the scheduled release date. Additionally, you will not be able to change the schedule release date (move up, delay, release now, or unpublish).
Eligibility and requirements

  • Eligibility. Only new KDP print books are eligible to schedule a release date. The following book types are not eligible for scheduled release:Public domain books

  • Low-content books

  • eBooks

  • Previously-published books

  • Books that are scheduled for release with another publisher

  • If a scheduled release book doesn’t meet our guidelines, you won’t be able to resubmit the same book. Instead, you need to update the manuscript to meet our guidelines and publish it as a new submission.

  • If a scheduled release book meets our guidelines, but we find that information is missing or that updates are required, we will notify you about this, and after you submit the required changes, we will review your updates.

  • My book was previously published: This option is available for books that are not new publications. Books that are previously published are not eligible for scheduling a release. Learn more about eligibility requirements for scheduling a release.

  1. Go to your Bookshelf.

  • ** Status: What it means**
  • Scheduled Release - Draft: Information for your title has been entered, but the Publish your Book button has not been selected. If you have made updates to a title, submit them for publication. Learn more about how to submit changes.
  • Scheduled Release - In Review: Your title has been scheduled for release and is currently in review, you won’t be able to make changes to your book until it finishes our review process. Review times may vary and may take longer if publishing rights need to be verified. Learn more about our review timelines.
  • Scheduled Release – Preparing your files: We’re preparing your title for publishing. A confirmation email will be sent to you when your title status changes to Release Scheduled.
  • Release Scheduled: Your title’s release has been scheduled. Your title’s Amazon detail page will remain hidden until 12:00 AM GMT on the book’s scheduled release date.
  • Release Scheduled - With unpublished changes: You’ve entered new information for this title, but the updates haven’t been published. A previous version of your title is scheduled for release. Learn more about how to submit changes.
  • Release Scheduled - Updates In Review: KDP is reviewing the recent changes for your title, you won’t be able to make changes to your book until it finishes our review process. Review times might vary and may take longer if publishing rights need to be verified. Learn more about our review timelines.
  • Release Scheduled - Preparing your files: Your recent changes are being prepared for publishing. A confirmation email will be sent to you when your title status changes to Release Scheduled. You won’t be able to make changes to your book until it finishes our review process.
  • Release Scheduled - Ready for Release: Your title is ready for release on your scheduled date. You won’t be able to make changes to the book content/details, order author copies and/or unpublish your book as we prepare to make the detail page available to customers. You can publish updates after the book is released.

Setting up pre-orders

Setting up pre-orders

Setting up pre-orders

You can set up your pre-order via your Bookshelf. ##### Create an eBook pre-order To get started with creating an eBook pre-order, follow the below steps: 1. Go to your Bookshelf. 2. Click the + Create button. 3. Click Create eBook. 4. Enter the eBook details in the Kindle eBook Details page. 5. Under Pre-order, select Make my Kindle eBook available for Pre-order. 6. Choose your release date. You’ll see a timer for the pre-order’s submission due date.

Note:* the release date is in GMT and you can schedule the release date a year in advance.* 7. Click Save and continue to continue.

You can edit your eBook for pre-order while it’s in the ‘Pre-order Draft’ status. Remember to complete and submit your manuscript before the submission deadline. Check pre-order statuses for more information. ##### Submitting pre-order When you’re ready to submit your pre-order, you must upload your final manuscript file to publish the version of the eBook you want delivered to customers. Follow the instructions below to submit your pre-order: 1. Go to your Bookshelf. 2. Select the ellipsis button (“…”) under KINDLE EBOOK ACTIONS next to the eBook you want to update. 3. Choose Edit eBook content. 4. Under Manuscript, upload the manuscript file that contains the version of the eBook you want delivered to customers. 5. Select Save and continue after your manuscript successfully uploads. 6. Proceed to finish setting up your book. This includes your cover, and rights and pricing information. 7. Click Submit for pre-order.

To successfully submit your pre-order, you must click Submit for pre-order. If you do not make this selection, your pre-order will continue to be in “Draft” status. Note: If you haven’t uploaded a manuscript and your pre-order is in “Draft” status, you must upload your final manuscript and submit your pre-order at least 72 hours before the submission deadline. If you do not submit your pre-order before the deadline, the pre-order will be canceled. You’ll lose the ability to edit your eBook and can’t set up new pre-orders for a year. Our customer service team cannot unlock your eBook title after the submission deadline. ##### Pre-order review process After you submit your pre-order, it will go through the review process. We review your book to ensure it meets our content guidelines. - If a pre-order book doesn’t meet our guidelines, you won’t be able to resubmit the same book. Instead, you need to update the manuscript to meet our guidelines and publish it as a new submission. - If the pre-order meets the guidelines, but we find that information is missing or that updates are required, we will notify you about this. After you submit the required changes, we will review your updates.

We encourage you to finish setting up your pre-order early in the event that changes are needed to meet our publishing guidelines. Refer to pre-order timelines for additional information. ###### Related articles - Pre-order timelines - Pre-order statuses - Reschedule a release - Delay or cancel a release

KDP Select
  • When will…: Timeline
  • My free promotion start and end?: Start and end dates are usually midnight Pacific Time.* For example, if you enter a start date of January 3 and an end date of January 7, your deal will begin at midnight on January 3 and run for four days (January 3, 4, 5 and 6) until it ends at midnight on January 7.
  • My free promotion end? I stopped it.: If you stop a free promotion in progress, the free promotion will generally end within a few minutes to few hours after you select Stop, but in some cases this period may be longer.
  • I be able to schedule my free promotion?: Promotions must be scheduled at least the day before your desired start date, but you can schedule them as far in advance as you would like. For example, if you want to begin a promotion on January 1, you can schedule it at any time up until December 31. If you schedule your promotion the day before you want it to begin, it may take up to four hours after the promotion is scheduled for it to begin. Any promotions scheduled before 8:00 p.m. Pacific Time the day before their scheduled start date will begin at approximately midnight. Anything scheduled after 8:00 p.m. Pacific time that day will begin within four hours of the time it was scheduled.
  • I be able to update a Live book scheduled for a free promotion?: You can update your Live book at any time.
  • My KDP Select–enrolled book be renewed?: Every KDP Select–enrolled title will be automatically renewed every 90 days from the time you first enrolled it, unless you opt out through the KDP website before the next renewal.
  • I be paid my share of the KDP Select Global Fund? There was no announcement.: You will be paid your share, in full, within 60 days for the preceding month’s activity.
  • I be able to schedule my Kindle Countdown Deal?: Kindle Countdown Deals must be scheduled 24 hours before your desired start date or as far in advance as you want. For example, to begin a promotion on January 10, you can schedule it any time before January 9.

Troubleshoot ISBN errors

Troubleshoot ISBN errors

If you’re using your own ISBN and get an error message, asking you to “Please fix the highlighted issue” but you don’t see any fields highlighted, this typically means there’s an issue with your ISBN or imprint. ISBN or imprint errors can occur in two scenarios: 1. There’s a spelling, spacing, or punctuation mistake. These fields are case-sensitive. All details must match exactly between KDP and the ISBN agency you used (e.g. Bowker).

Solution: We recommend copying and pasting directly from the ISBN agency into KDP.

  1. Solution: Go to the ISBN agency’s website and review the imprint name, title, and author associated with the ISBN. Verify the details match between KDP and them.

Tip: Most authors use Bowker. If you have questions about your ISBN metadata, you’ll need to contact them. ##### Errors after updating ISBN info on Bowker If you recently changed your ISBN details, and are trying to update your book details in KDP, you may need to wait a few days for us to register the changes from Bowker. It can take up to 5 business days for KDP to pick up changes on Bowker. After this timeline, you can save your book updates and submit for publishing.

  10. Click Launch Previewer.

  11. A quality panel will expand from the right side of the Online Previewer. You can close the panel to hide quality issues in the preview. The panel can be opened anytime by clicking the Quality button located at the top right corner.

  12. What you will see in the side-panel:

Email Issues. The list of issues will be emailed to your KDP account email address. 9. Ignore All. You can choose to ignore quality issues. Ignored issues won’t be shown the next time you upload your manuscript. Note: Even if you ignored the issues listed, your eBook will still go through our regular publishing process. The side-panel can detect low quality images that can appear blurry on Kindle devices. 13. Language mismatch. Spell Check and Image Check are available in Online Previewer for English eBooks only. 14. Wrong Layout. The side-panel only supports eBooks with reflowable format.

  1. Open the Online Previewer and click the Quality option located at the top right corner.

If you want to fix errors that are not highlighted in the side-panel, you will need to make the necessary edits in the original source file (HTML, EPUB, DOCX, etc.) and upload it directly to KDP. 1. Under “Downloadable Preview Options,” click Preview on your computer and follow the steps to download your file.

You can also preview your file on your computer with Kindle Previewer. What is an ISBN and Imprint?

What is an ISBN and Imprint?

What is an ISBN and Imprint?

When publishing a book with KDP, you’ll be asked to provide an ISBN and imprint (i.e. publisher). This article explains what an ISBN and imprint are, while detailing requirements for publishing. ##### What is an ISBN? An ISBN (International Standard Book Number) is a unique identifier for books. It helps bookstores, libraries, distributors, and readers find and reference your book correctly. Each format of your book (paperback vs hardcover) needs its own ISBN. eBooks and low-content books are the only formats where an ISBN is optional. The same ISBN cannot be reused across multiple book formats or new editions that introduce significant changes from the original version. KDP allows two options for ISBNs: 1. You can use a free ISBN from KDP (paperback and hardcover books only). 2. You can purchase your own ISBN.

Note: - Free ISBNs from us can only be used on KDP. They cannot be used to publish outside of KDP. - Hardcover is currently unsupported in JP.

If you purchase your own ISBN, you must enter the same details (i.e. book title, author name, publisher) in KDP that you used to register the ISBN. ##### What is an Imprint? An imprint is the name of the publisher associated with your book’s ISBN. If you buy your own ISBN, you can list your own publishing imprint (such as your business or brand name). If you use a free ISBN from KDP, the imprint will appear as “Independently published.” If you use your own ISBN, KDP will check whether your book’s imprint matches what’s on file with the ISBN agency (e.g. Bowker). If there’s a mismatch, you won’t be able to publish. Note: - Entering ISBN and imprint details are case-sensitive. Even extra spaces at the end of the imprint name can cause mismatch errors. Do not enter placeholders, such as “unknown” or “n/a.” - The Imprint field has a limit of 100 characters.

Write a Book Description

Write a Book Description

Contents
  • How to write your book description
  • How to enter your book description
  • Formatting your book description
  • Supported HTML in your book description
  • Finished example description with HTML

How to write your book description
  • Simple Describe the main plot, theme, or idea only. Avoid details that may overwhelm or confuse a reader who’s only taking a second or two to decide whether to find out more about your book. Also, keep your language short and simple. Aim for a 150-word paragraph with sentences that are easy to scan.
  • Compelling

Avoiding overwhelming and confusing details will help make your description compelling, but also consider how to grab readers’ attention. For example, write a first sentence that draws them in. This sentence may be a reader’s first impression, so make it special. Also, set expectations by showing what genre your book belongs to. - Professional Again, this might be your reader’s first impression, so make sure your description is polished–no misspellings or grammatical errors. It may be hard to edit a text you’ve looked at several times, so show it to others to get a fresh set of eyes.

How to enter your book description
  1. Sign in to: https://kdp.amazon.com
  2. Go to your Bookshelf
  3. Next to the book you want to update, click the ellipsis button (“…”).
  4. Select Edit Details.
  5. Under Description, make the necessary edits. Note that we have a limit of 4000 characters for the description.
  6. Click Save and Continue.
  7. At the bottom of the Pricing page, click Publish.
Formatting your book description
  • If you use double or multiple spaces between words within the editor, this will not be reflected on your detail page.
  • Single, angled brackets can be used after text or in conjunction with their opposite. Multiple brackets used alone are also not supported. Here are examples of what’s supported: Allowed:
  • Not allowed: < text
  • Not allowed: << OR >>
  • Not allowed: <>OR <> <>

          Delete a series

          Delete a series

          Remove a book or delete a series

          Contents
          • Remove book from series
          • Delete series
          Remove book from series
          1. Go to your Bookshelf.
          2. Find a book in the series and click Manage title.
          3. Click Manage series.
          4. Scroll to the book in the series you want to remove and click Series Actions.
          5. Choose Remove from series.
          Delete Series
          1. Follow the instructions to remove the titles from your series.
          2. From the Manage series page, click Manage series.
          3. Choose Delete Series.
          4. Click Delete series to delete the Amazon series page and remove the series from your KDP account. After you delete a series, you won’t be able to view the Series Manager page.

          Edit your Series

          Edit your Series

          Edit your Series

          Contents
          • Edit series details
          • Add existing book
          • Create new book
          • Edit series relationship
          Edit series details
          1. Go to your Bookshelf.
          2. Find the book in the series you want to edit and click Manage title.
          3. Click Manage series.
          4. Click Edit series details.
          5. Make your changes.
          6. Click Submit updates to publish changes to your Amazon series page.
          Add existing book
          1. Go to your Bookshelf.
          2. Find a book in the series and click Manage title.
          3. Click Manage Series.
          4. From that page, click +Add existing title.
          5. Follow the steps to select a book to add to your series.
          Create a new book
          1. Go to your Bookshelf.
          2. Find a book in the series and click Manage title.
          3. Click Manage Series.
          4. From that page, click + Create new Title.
          5. Follow the steps to create a book and add to your series.
          Edit series relationship
          1. Go to your Bookshelf.
          2. Find a book in the series and click Manage title.
          3. Click Manage Series.
          4. Click Main Content and Related Content to check the book’s relationship.
          5. Scroll to the book you want to edit and click Series Actions.
          6. Choose Edit Series relationship.
          7. Follow the steps to update your title to main or related content.
          8. Click Done to confirm the changes.

          Create or update a Series Collection
          1. Go to your Bookshelf and click Create new title. For existing titles, go to your Bookshelf and click the ellipsis button (“…”) under the “eBook Actions” or “Paperback Actions” menu next to your book. Then, choose Edit eBook Details or Edit Paperback Details accordingly.
          2. In the Book Title field, enter the title of your book. For example, The Two Towers.
          3. In the Subtitle (optional) field, provide the subtitle if it exists. If the book does not have a subtitle, leave it blank. Don’t add any series information in this field.
          4. Under Series, in the Series name field, enter the name of the series. For example, The Lord of the Rings. To ensure all books in your series appear on the Series Collection page, you must use the exact series name for all books. For example, The Lord of the Rings does not match Lord of the Rings
          5. In the Series number field, enter the series number for the book. eBooks in an ordered series without a series number won’t appear on your Series Collection page. If you’re creating an unordered series (US only), you can leave this field blank and your titles will appear by publication date.
          6. After you publish or republish all eBooks in the series with accurate series information, contact us with the list of ASINs you want us to include on the Series Collection page.

          Edit book order
          1. Go to your Bookshelf.

          5. Click Edit and change the number to update the order in which you want the books to appear on the series page.
          6. Click Update.
          7. Click Save and publish order to update the book order on your Amazon series page.

          What you should know
          • Enroll in KDP Select to earn up to 70% royalty on sales, as well as a share of the KDP Select global fund when a customer uses Kindle Unlimited to read your eBook.
          • Distribute your eBook to worldwide Kindle stores.
          • We’re still improving our support for eBooks written in Arabic, but we welcome publishers with Arabic content. You may encounter errors when uploading a manuscript. See Step 4 in the section “How to format your eBook in Word” below for tips.
          • If you choose to receive payments via wire transfer to your local bank in Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Morocco, you will be paid in local currencies (e.g. Saudi Riyals, Oman Rials, Bahraini Dinars, Kuwaiti Dinars, and Moroccan Dirham).
          • Paperback publishing for the Arabic language isn’t currently available.
          • Send us feedback or ask us questions! Tell us which file formats you’d like us to support, or any other improvements you’d like to request.
          Getting started on KDP
          • Account setup
          • Publishing overview
          How to format your eBook in Word
          • (image: Step 1): Step 1: Format your title page Your eBook should include a title page with your book title and author name. You can also add other front matter pages like a copyright and dedication page, but these aren’t required. Make sure the information on your title page exactly matches the book details you entered title setup. Mismatches are one of the most common reasons files are rejected.
          • (image: Step 2): Step 2: Indent paragraphs, set line spacing, and page breaks

          Go to your first chapter and highlight all your paragraphs. Go to the Home tab and open the Paragraph dialog box by clicking the small diagonal arrow at the bottom right of the “Paragraph” section. Under “Indentation,” select First line from the “Special” drop-down menu. In the “By” field, enter 0.2” (5 mm). Under “Spacing,” set “Before” and “After” to 0 pt. Select Single from the “Line spacing” drop-down menu and click OK. Click where the chapter text ends and click Page Break. Repeat these steps for each chapter. - (image: Step 3): Step 3: Create an active table of contents An active table of contents is one of the features eBook readers need and expect. Why? Because the table of contents lets them to jump to specific places in the book by clicking on links embedded in the text. eBooks don’t have page numbers, and page counts change when the reader adjusts the text size. To create an active table of contents:

          Go to your first chapter and highlight the chapter title. Go to the Home tab, and in the “Styles” section, click Heading 1. If you want, add additional formatting (e.g., alignment, bold text, or font size). Repeat these steps for each chapter. Be sure to apply any additional formatting consistently. Click where you want to insert your table of contents. Go to the References tab and click Table of Contents. Select Automatic Table 1. Click Table of Contents again, but this time select Custom Table of Contents. Uncheck the Show Page Numbers box, set “Show levels” to 1, and click OK. When asked if you want to replace the table of contents, click Yes. Highlight the table of contents title “Contents.” Go to the Insert tab, and in the “Links” section, click Bookmark. Enter “toc” (without the quotation marks) into the “Bookmark name” field and click Add. Insert a page break after your table of contents. - (image: Step 4): Step 4: Preview your eBook Before you upload your eBook to KDP, check out the tips below, and make any necessary updates to your file. These tips include the most common reasons Arabic files are rejected. Also see our Help page for details on our quality guidelines.

          We recommend reviewing your eBook in Kindle Previewer, a desktop application that shows you how your eBook will look on tablets, Kindle E-readers, and phones. Previewer can help you find and fix formatting and typographical errors.

          See the table below for our top tips:

          Tip 1: Make sure text direction is set to right-to-left: Arabic is a “right-to-left” language, so we’ll reject files set to left-to-right. To check the text direction in Word:

          Go to the File tab. Choose Options, and click Language. In the “Choose Editing Languages” section, add the Arabic dialect you want. Click Add. - Tip 2: Check for typos: Common typos in Arabic-language eBooks include:

          Text rendered as a tofu box (e.g., ) Numbers in place of letters and vice versa (e.g., يعود تاريخ السويد الحديثة إلى عام ٢٣ه١) Incorrectly placed Tashkeel (e.g., أنِا طالب instead of أنَا طالب) Irregular spacing between in letters between words (e.g., بدأ ن ش ر روايته الجديدة أولاد حارتنا في جريدة الأهرام) Extra character added in word (e.g., وأنا لن أتمنى لوك)

          Found a typo in your eBook? Look for the term throughout your file to ensure all occurrences are corrected. The search function in Kindle Previewer can help you find and fix all instances. - Tip 3: Remove promotional, inappropriate, and disappointing content: Review your eBook for content like ads, barcodes, and links to commercial eBook store sites or competitor websites. We do not allow content that misleads or disappoints our customers, including content whose primary purpose is to solicit or advertise.

          If you find content like this, remove it from your entire book. The search function in Kindle Previewer can help you find and remove all instances. See our content and quality guidelines. - Tip 4: Check the book details you entered during title setup: Make sure you chose “Arabic” from the menu in the “Language” section of the Kindle eBook Details page. The language you choose and the language in which the eBook is written must match.

          Also make sure that the book details (e.g., title, author name) you entered are in Arabic. The language you choose and the language in which the book details are entered must match. - Tip 5: Make sure your book consists primarily of text: Your eBook should be reflowable and consist primarily of text, not scanned pages from a physical book. Your readers won’t be able to change text size in the scans.

          Book Supported Languages

          • Content uploaded in an eBook-only language cannot be converted into a paperback book.

          • eBook content uploaded in an unsupported language won’t display properly on Kindle devices and will be removed from sale.

          • Select the language in your Bookshelf that matches the language of the written content to prevent file rejection.

          • Content uploaded in a paperback-only language cannot be converted into a Kindle eBook or hardcover book.

          • Standard color distribution for right-to-left (RTL) paperbacks is limited to Amazon.co.jp.

Additionally, XDMF format is available for Japanese publishers.           Chinese (Traditional) (Beta)

          • Format your eBook with horizontal content, not vertical content.

          • Format your eBook with content that’s read from left to right (LTR), not right to left (RTL).

          Indian-Language Publishing

          Indian-Language Publishing

          What you should know
          • Paperback publishing for Indian languages is not available at this time. Learn more about the languages we support.
          • We recommend using English for the book details (e.g., title, author name) you enter when setting up your title. KDP accepts Indian languages, but they may not display correctly on all Amazon and Kindle websites, apps, and emails.
          • KDP currently accepts Indian language content only in Microsoft Word (.doc/docx) formats.
          • Enroll in KDP Select to earn up to 70% royalty on sales to Amazon.in, as well as a share of the KDP Select global fund when a customer uses Kindle Unlimited to read your book.
          • Distribute your book to worldwide Kindle stores including Amazon.in, Amazon.com (US), and Amazon.co.uk (UK).
          • We’re still improving our support for these languages. You may encounter errors when uploading a manuscript. Learn more about fixing common file conversion issues.

          Publishing in Hebrew, Persian, and Yiddish

          Publishing in Hebrew, Persian, and Yiddish

          Hebrew and Yiddish

          What you should know about paperbacks and hardcovers:
          • Hardcover publishing for Hebrew and Yiddish in right-to-left (RTL) isn’t currently available.
          • The standard color option is not available for these languages.
          • Hebrew and Yiddish paperbacks are not currently eligible for Expanded Distribution.
          • Upload your interior as a PDF file. We don’t support other file types for Hebrew and Yiddish.
          • Upload your cover as a PDF file. Cover Creator is not available for Hebrew and Yiddish.
          Submitting your Hebrew and Yiddish interior and cover
          1. Go to the File tab.
          2. Choose Options, and click Language.
          3. In the “Choose Editing Languages” section, add either Hebrew or Yiddish.
          4. Click Add.
          What you should know about eBooks:
          • Yiddish isn’t currently available for eBook publishing.
          • Kindle for Web does not support right-to-left languages (Arabic/Hebrew/Persian).
          • X-Ray, WordWise, and page numbers are not available for these languages.
          • Upload your manuscript in .doc/docx or EPUB format.
          • For Persian eBooks: Character spacing is not supported, so manuscripts should be formatted without relying on character spacing.
          Submitting your Hebrew and Persian manuscripts:
          1. Select your language (Arabic, Hebrew, or Persian) from the language menu during title setup.
          2. Enter your book details, such as title, author name, etc.
          3. Upload your manuscript in .doc/docx or EPUB format. It must be formatted to match the reading direction.
          4. Upload a cover image matching the reading direction. Use the ‘Previewer’ for file or formatting issues.
